docs.title: sidescanpy
docs.text:
Read, correct, grid and export sidescan sonar data.

sidescanpy converts EdgeTech JSF, Klein SDF and XTF surveys into one xarray-based model stored as .ss.h5, then corrects it (TVG, ground range, georeferencing), slices it, grids it to rasters and GeoTIFF, and builds COCO/YOLO training datasets from target catalogs. Small analysis functions measure a dataset's units, nadir, usable range and TVG state.

Pre-release

Until 1.0, any 0.x release may change the .ss.h5 file format, the API and the CLI. Keep your raw sonar files, pin the version you use, and expect to re-convert .ss.h5 files after an upgrade. See Pre-release status.

A public EdgeTech recording, raw (left) and after the bottom track, TVG and slant-to-ground-range steps (right). Code and data: Correct a line.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
from sidescanpy import datasets
from sidescanpy.grids import grid_channel, to_geotiff
from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert
from sidescanpy.io.hdf5 import write_survey
from sidescanpy.processing import correct_survey

# A public Benthos XTF line; any JSF, SDF or XTF path works the same way.
path = datasets.fetch("jncc_mid_irish_sea_MIS11_0.xtf")
survey = read_and_convert([path], fmt="xtf")

# Navigation onto pings, TVG, slant to ground range, per-sample lat/lon.
survey = correct_survey(survey)
write_survey(survey, "MIS11_0.ss.h5")

# Grid one frequency at 1 m and write a GeoTIFF (needs the geo extra).
raster = grid_channel(survey.get_frequency("hz_400000").dataset, resolution_m=1.0)
to_geotiff(raster, "MIS11_0_400khz.tif")

Installing is covered in Pre-release status.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Examples: real data, code and results, all on openly licensed recordings you can download.
  • Guide: Building a workflow, Data model, Processing, Gridding, Targets and datasets, Analysis, Visualization, Command line, Logging.
  • Formats: JSF, SDF, XTF, HDF5, NetCDF.
  • Reference: API reference, one page per module, generated from the docstrings.

docs.title: Analysis
docs.text:
sidescanpy.analysis measures a dataset. Each function takes data and returns a dataclass with a to_dict(); none of them writes files, plots or decides what to do next. Plots for each result are in sidescanpy.viz (Visualization); sidescan-analyze investigate and examples/investigate_dataset.py run them all on one file and write a report.

Function Answers characterize_values data type, shape and distribution of a variable infer_units raw counts, dB, volts or normalized, from the value range compare_outlier_rejection distribution before and after processing.reject_range_outliers analyze_nadir nadir type (gap, bright spike, noisy, clean), altitude sample and first bottom return estimate_beam_geometry near-edge and far-edge beam angles, beam width estimate_usable_range where the signal falls into the noise floor fit_range_decay which loss terms are already compensated in the data: none, spreading_only, absorption_only, full, or ambiguous fit_tvg_curve fits of the four candidate loss models to a binned dB-vs-range curve compare_before_after raw and TVG-corrected backscatter side by side bin_by_altitude pings split into equal-count altitude bins summarize_navigation per-field navigation/attitude statistics and a heading-convention check measure_ping_geometry median ping spacing, swath width and sample interval detect_shadow_proposals object proposal boxes (native ping, sample, side) from acoustic shadows and the highlight in front of them, with sizes, contrast, estimated height and a score

Analysis that needs the uncorrected signal recovers it with processing.uncorrected_backscatter, so it works on corrected files.

docs.title: Reading the results
docs.text:
• A best fit in fit_range_decay is a hypothesis. Apply the winning correction and check that the corrected data is flat over the fit window before trusting it, especially when the window is short.
  • A smooth per-ping boundary is not proof of a correct one: a detector stuck at a floor value is also smooth. Compare port and starboard, or two frequencies, when a result looks too clean.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
Four commands cover quick runs; each subcommand calls one library function. Run any of them with --help for the full option list.

Command Subcommands sidescan-convert survey (JSF/SDF/XTF → .ss.h5, one file per input, except XTF files whose range setting changes, which give one <stem>_seg01.ss.h5, <stem>_seg02.ss.h5, … per constant-range run, runs shorter than --min-segment-pings (50) dropped; far-range noise cropped per output unless --no-crop-farrange), targets (catalog → targets.json/.csv; --plot adds a position scatter) sidescan-correct applies --crop-farrange, --tvg, --geometric, --range-correction, --georef to every .ss.h5 in --ss-h5-dir, in place; TVG terms via --spreading-loss-db, --absorption-db-per-m, --no-spreading, --no-absorption, water conditions via --temperature-c --salinity-psu --depth-m --ph; --ping-chunk-size bounds memory sidescan-export waterfall, grid (--geotiff), track, chip (COCO/YOLO dataset, see Targets and datasets) sidescan-analyze investigate (every analysis + report), tvg-fit, segment, nadir, beam-geometry, usable-range, units, nav-attitude (alias nav-summary), recommend-config

docs.title: Config files
docs.text: Every subcommand takes --config file.yaml (or .json). Keys are the option names with underscores (spreading_loss_db: 30); flags on the command line override them. Keys the subcommand does not have log a warning, so one config file can be shared across commands; --strict-config turns the warning into an error.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: -v shows library DEBUG messages, -q shows warnings only, and --log-file PATH also writes the log to a file.

docs.title: Without matplotlib
docs.text: sidescan-convert and sidescan-correct run without the [viz] extra. sidescan-export and sidescan-analyze need it for figures; analysis subcommands with --no-plots and recommend-config do not.

docs.title: Core schema and survey
docs.text: The core module defines the data contract used everywhere else in SideScanPy and provides the top-level types user code interacts with.

docs.title: The two-layer model
docs.text:
SideScanSurvey                                     ← multi-frequency container
├── freq_channels: dict[str, SideScanFrequencyChannel]
│       │
│       └── dataset: xr.Dataset                    ← validated single-frequency
│               ├─ dims: ping × channel × sample
│               ├─ coords: ping_number, time, channel_id
│               └─ vars: backscatter_*, lat, lon, heading, ...
│
└── aux records (xr.Datasets)
    ├── navigation                                 ← ds.navigation_record
    ├── attitude                                   ← ds.attitude_record
    ├── dvl                                        ← ds.dvl_record
    └── sensors: dict[str, xr.Dataset]             ← ds.sensor_record

A frequency channel is a single ping-time-indexed dataset for one acoustic frequency. A survey holds one or more channels plus auxiliary streams (navigation, attitude, DVL, sensors) that are sampled on their own timestamps — independent of pings — and shared across all frequencies.

Aux records live at the survey level (not the channel level) because they describe the platform, not the sonar. The same GPS fixes apply to every frequency the towfish was pinging at the same time.

docs.title: Schema validation
docs.text:
Every dataset is validated by an xarray accessor on construction or assignment. A dataset that doesn't conform raises ValueError with a message naming the missing piece.

Accessor Used on Required vars ds.sidescan Single-frequency channel backscatter_intensity, latitude, longitude, heading_deg, depth_m, roll_deg, pitch_deg, heave_m, altitude_m, sound_vel_ms, fathometer_reading_m ds.navigation_record Navigation aux latitude, longitude ds.attitude_record Attitude aux roll_deg, pitch_deg, heave_m ds.dvl_record DVL aux altitude_m ds.sensor_record Generic sensor aux (none, sensor-dependent)

Required dims, coords, and attrs are listed in schema.py. The sidescan schema enforces channel size 2 (port + starboard). The processing level (raw, tvg, geometric, range_correction, georef) is derived from the recorded steps by core.history.processing_level(), not stored separately.

docs.title: Validation is eager
docs.text: SideScanFrequencyChannel.__init__ runs ds.sidescan.validate(). Aux record setters on SideScanSurvey validate before assigning. Bad data fails fast with a specific message — there's no "you can stuff anything in and it'll fail later" mode.

docs.title: Empty-but-valid aux records
docs.text:
Aux records can be empty (zero obs) and still pass validation. This matters for round-trip serialization: surveys without nav messages still write a nav group on disk, which loads back as an empty record. The is_empty() method on each aux accessor reports this. The SideScanSurvey.has_navigation (etc.) shortcut returns False for both None and empty.

The make_empty_*_record() helpers in schema.py build these zero-obs datasets when needed.

docs.title: Survey container
docs.text:
SideScanSurvey is a thin container with a few useful conventions:

  • Frequencies are added by string key (e.g. "hz_1495000") via add_frequency(key, dataset). Overwriting warns.
  • Aux records are exposed as @property + @setter pairs: setting survey.navigation = ds validates and assigns; setting it to None clears.
  • Sensors are keyed by sensor_type and accessed via add_sensor(type, ds) and get_sensor(type).
  • Derived properties (time_range, bounding_box, frequency_hz_list, etc.) compute on demand. The bounding box prefers the navigation aux record when populated, falling back to per-ping lat/lon arrays otherwise.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• All time coords are datetime64[ns]. Builders that produce time arrays from pandas may need .astype("datetime64[ns]") because pandas 2.x defaults to [us].
  • processing_level advances through the pipeline: raw → radiometric → geometric → georeferenced. Functions assert their expected input level and update the attribute on output.
  • processing_history is a JSON-encoded list. Each entry has step, timestamp_utc, params, function, version. Use ds.sidescan.append_to_history(...) rather than building entries by hand.
  • The channel_id coord is always ["port", "starboard"] as native Python strings (the HDF5/NetCDF readers normalize byte-strings back to native strings).

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Add tests for the aux stream accessors (currently only the main sidescan accessor has dedicated tests; aux validation is covered indirectly through round-trip and converter tests).
  • Add a SideScanSurvey.replace_frequency(key, ds) method so callers don't have to reach into _freq_channels for in-place channel updates.
  • Add a SideScanSurvey.clone() method for deep copying when needed (currently interpolate.py::_shallow_copy_survey does this manually).
  • Optional: add processing_level validation that prevents going backwards (e.g. raw → radiometric is allowed; radiometric → raw is not).
  • Document the HDF5_* constants in their own section once docs/io_hdf5.md exists, then remove the duplication here.

docs.title: Target catalogs
docs.text:
sidescanpy.targets.Target describes one picked contact: id, position (lat/lon and/or ping/channel/sample), optional measured bbox, position_confidence (unknown < approximate < verified) and category.

Function Purpose io.read_target_catalog(dir) read an EdgeTech *.target or Klein Target_*.tgt catalog from a directory targets.read_targets_json / write_targets_json (and _csv) the format-agnostic catalog file targets.correlate.build_position_index(ss_h5_dir) cache per-ping positions of every .ss.h5 targets.correlate.correlate_target(target, index, max_dist_m) the closest ping (geodesic distance) across files and frequencies targets.correlate.correlate_catalog / place_catalog the same for a whole catalog, grouped by file, frequency and channel targets.correlate.resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping(targets, ss_h5_dir) Klein: place each target at the ping its catalog names (catalog ping time + number, no clock offset) targets.correlate.calibrate_clock_offset estimate a constant clock offset between a catalog's pick times and the survey (fallback for catalogs without ping fields)

docs.title: Native-resolution windows
docs.text:
export.windows.native cuts windows that are square (chips) or a fixed length (tiles) in metres from the native ping x sample grid and resizes them with linear interpolation, for sonars whose ping spacing is much coarser than their sample spacing:

Function Purpose native_chip(ds, ping=, channel=, sample=, size_m=, size_px=) one side, centred on a target swath_tiles(ds, tile_m=, px_m=, overlap_m=) the whole channel as dual-swath tiles (port mirrored left) NativeWindow.to_pixel / to_native / box_to_native map between image pixels and (ping, sample, channel), e.g. to turn annotation boxes back into sonar coordinates

docs.title: Building a dataset
docs.text:
export.ml.build_target_dataset(sources, targets, spec, out_dir) renders one image per target per style and writes COCO (targets.coco.json) and YOLO (labels/, data.yaml) annotations. Everything that shapes the dataset lives in one DatasetSpec, which round-trips to YAML.

DatasetSpec field Meaning styles chip (fixed crop on one channel), single-swath (one channel's full swath), dual-swath (both channels) render_level uncorrected, db or radiometric (native pixels); geometric or georef (real-world meters) size_px, swath_size_px output size, square resolution_m meters per pixel for geometric/georef; a list renders each value as its own dataset across_axis ground (ground range) or slant (slant range, no ground projection) for geometric swath_fill size swath frames to the across-track extent the data fills (no black margins) resample_method griddata, kdtree or binned for geometric jitter_px, n_augment, random_flip, seed augmentation: random offset of the target in the frame, draws per target, random horizontal/vertical flips box_size, box_size_m placeholder box for targets with no measured extent (pixels, or meters converted per image) categories, min_confidence class names, and which targets get annotations n_background, background_margin_m, background_max_nan_frac, background_ping_ranges background (no-target) images: windows whose footprint plus margin contains no catalog target val_fraction, split_block_pings, layout train/val split (targets by id hash, backgrounds by file and ping block) and flat or ultralytics folder layout bit_depth, gamma, pct_low, pct_high, normalization_scope how values become 8- or 16-bit pixels

Each run writes manifest.json and returns a DatasetResult with per-style counts and the targets that were skipped and why.

Background images are only as clean as the catalog: an object missing from the catalog can appear in a background image and will be learned as background.

docs.title: Lower-level pieces
docs.text:
sidescanpy.export also exposes the building blocks: window extraction (extract_chip, extract_full_channel, extract_geometric_window*, extract_georef_window), orientation (orient_pixel_window, orient_geo_window), augmentation (random_flip, jitter_offset_m), quantization (to_uint8, to_uint16, from_uint8), and export.ml.write_coco / write_yolo.

sidescan-export chip is a thin command-line wrapper over build_target_dataset; examples/build_yolo_dataset.py runs end to end on a synthetic survey.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv for package management (recommended) or pip
  • Git

docs.title: Initial Setup
docs.text:
# Clone repo
git clone <repo-url>
cd sidescanpy

# Create virtual environment with uv
uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install in editable mode with dev dependencies
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

# Verify installation
pytest tests/unit/ -v

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text: See CLAUDE.md for detailed architecture overview.

docs.title: Making Changes
docs.text:
1. Read CLAUDE.md — Project context and current focus
  2. Write a design note first if it's a big change (kept outside the repo)
  3. Write tests first — TDD is preferred
  4. Implement — Small, focused changes
  5. Run tests — pytest tests/unit/ -v
  6. Commit — Conventional Commits format
  7. Update CLAUDE.md — If current focus or architecture changed

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
# Fast unit tests
pytest tests/unit/ -v

# Integration tests (requires fixtures)
pytest tests/integration/ -v --slow

# Coverage
pytest tests/unit/ --cov=sidescanpy --cov-report=html

# Specific test
pytest tests/unit/grids/test_resample.py::TestResampleChannelToGrid3DValidation -v

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• Type hints: Use for public APIs
  • Docstrings: NumPy style for functions/classes
  • Line length: 100 characters (soft limit)
  • Imports: Standard library first, then third-party, then local

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
Follow Conventional Commits:

<type>(<scope>): <description>

[optional body]

[optional footer]

Types: feat, fix, test, docs, refactor, perf, chore

Scopes: Use hyphenated module paths (e.g., io/sdf, grids/resample)

Examples: - feat(grids): add resample_channel_to_grid for 3D data - fix(io/jsf): correct navigation timestamp parsing - test(grids): add fixtures for 3D channel data - docs(readme): update installation instructions

docs.title: Running Examples
docs.text:
Scripts in examples/ run on synthetic data and are smoke-tested in tests/examples/.

python examples/quickstart.py

docs.title: Working with Claude Code
docs.text:
This project is set up for use with Claude Code.

  • Project context: CLAUDE.md (read automatically at session start)
  • Prompts: .claude/prompts/ (feature planning, TDD, refactoring templates)

docs.text:
1. Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md — includes current work focus
  2. Plan work (a design note outside the repo if complex)
  3. Implement with TDD approach
  4. Run tests after each change
  5. Suggest commits (user approves and commits manually)
  6. Update CLAUDE.md at session end if focus changed
