docs.title: Sharing before release
docs.text:
Until the public release the repository is private and shared by invitation. Pre-release status is the page for the people invited; this section is the maintainer's side.

Repository. It lives in the rshomberg-research organization (moved from a personal account, where collaborators always get write access). Add people as outside collaborators with the Read role: Settings → Collaborators and teams. If it moves again, update origin in each clone, [project.urls] in pyproject.toml, repo_url in mkdocs.yml, and the links in README.md and docs/ (grep -rn "github.com/" README.md docs mkdocs.yml pyproject.toml).

Before inviting anyone, everything on GitHub (every branch, tag and commit message) is visible to them. Check it holds nothing that should stay private, with the names to look for in place of the placeholders:

git fetch origin --tags --force
git log --remotes=origin --tags -p -i -G"<name>|<other name>" --format="%h %s"
git log --remotes=origin --tags -i --grep="<name>" --format="%h %s"

Docs. The site is public at https://rshomberg-research.github.io/sidescanpy/ while the code stays private. GitHub Pages can't serve a private repository on the organization's free plan, so the docs workflow pushes each build of main into the sidescanpy/ folder of the public repository rshomberg-research/rshomberg-research.github.io, which Pages serves. The workflow also keeps every build of main and of v* tags as the sidescanpy-docs artifact (90 days).

One-time setup, as an organization owner:

# 1. The public site repository: a redirect to the docs, served by Pages.
gh repo create rshomberg-research/rshomberg-research.github.io --public \
   --description "Public site of rshomberg-research (sidescanpy docs)"
#    push an index.html that redirects to sidescanpy/ and an empty .nojekyll,
#    then: Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> main, / (root)

# 2. A deploy key the docs workflow pushes with.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N "" -C "sidescanpy docs deploy" -f docs_deploy_key
gh repo deploy-key add docs_deploy_key.pub --allow-write \
   -R rshomberg-research/rshomberg-research.github.io --title "sidescanpy docs"
gh secret set DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY -R rshomberg-research/sidescanpy < docs_deploy_key
rm docs_deploy_key docs_deploy_key.pub

# 3. Turn publishing on; the next push to main publishes.
gh variable set PUBLISH_DOCS --body true -R rshomberg-research/sidescanpy

Everything on the site is public, including the API reference built from the docstrings (signatures and docstrings, not source), the example scripts and the development guide. Until the release the pages carry a noindex tag (overrides/main.html), so the link works for the people it is given to but search engines leave it out. At the public release, enable Pages on this repository instead (same URL), remove sidescanpy/ from the site repository, and delete overrides/ and custom_dir in mkdocs.yml.

Gallery. make gallery re-runs examples/gallery/ and refreshes the images in docs/assets/gallery/ (the README uses two of them). The scripts download real data, so they are not run in CI; CI only checks that every dataset name they fetch is registered.

Test data. The public fixtures are shared as one zip, through a link-shared folder that each invited person is added to. Rebuild it whenever a fixture or SOURCES.md changes:

cd /path/to/fixtures/..       # the directory holding the fixtures folder
mkdir sidescanpy-public-fixtures
cp fixtures/*.jsf fixtures/*.xtf /path/to/sidescanpy/tests/data/public/SOURCES.md \
   sidescanpy-public-fixtures/
zip -qrX sidescanpy-public-fixtures-$(date +%F).zip sidescanpy-public-fixtures
rm -r sidescanpy-public-fixtures

Then run test_public_fixtures.py against the unzipped copy before uploading it. Only openly licensed data goes in the zip (see SOURCES.md). Don't mint a Zenodo DOI for the data before the public release: a published Zenodo record can't be withdrawn, and even a restricted one shows its metadata publicly.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text: Rough flow: 1. All work committed on feature branch 2. All tests passing 3. CHANGELOG.md updated 4. Version bumped in pyproject.toml 5. Merge to main 6. Tag: git tag v0.X.0 7. Update CLAUDE.md — new "Current Work" state 8. Push tag: git push origin v0.X.0

docs.title: Pre-tag checklist
docs.text:
Before running git tag vX.Y.Z:

Documentation - [ ] CHANGELOG.md has a dated section for the new version - [ ] New features documented in docs/ - [ ] README.md reflects supported formats and current capabilities - [ ] CLAUDE.md "Current Work Focus" updated to new state

Code quality - [ ] No stray print() debug statements - [ ] Logging levels appropriate (DEBUG / INFO / WARNING) - [ ] TODOs related to this version resolved or explicitly deferred

Tests - [ ] pytest tests/unit -v all green - [ ] pytest tests/integration -v --slow all green - [ ] No accidentally-skipped tests

Build & packaging - [ ] Version bumped in pyproject.toml - [ ] Version bumped in sidescanpy/__init__.py if __version__ exists - [ ] python -m build succeeds - [ ] Fresh-venv install of the wheel works

Git hygiene - [ ] All work committed - [ ] Working tree clean - [ ] Branch up to date with main

docs.title: Gridding
docs.text:
sidescanpy.grids resamples georeferenced backscatter onto a regular raster. The input needs latitude_per_sample / longitude_per_sample (the georef correction step).

from sidescanpy.grids import grid_channel, recommend_resolution, to_geotiff

res = recommend_resolution(ds)            # half the finer of ping spacing and sample interval
raster = grid_channel(ds, resolution_m=res, method="median")
to_geotiff(raster, "survey.tif")          # needs the [geo] extra

docs.title: Pieces
docs.text: Object Purpose GridDefinition bounding box, resolution and CRS of a grid utm_grid_from_wgs84_bbox(bbox, resolution_m) a grid in the UTM zone containing the bbox centre bbox_from_channel_dataset(ds) a padded (south, west, north, east) box around the data resample_channel_to_grid(ds, grid_def, method=...) the resampler grid_channel(ds, resolution_m, method) the two steps above in one call, on a UTM grid fit to the data SideScanGriddedRaster the result: an xr.Dataset wrapper holding backscatter, with its CRS, units, cell counts and data_coverage to_geotiff(raster, path) single-band GeoTIFF via rioxarray

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
ResamplingMethod: mean, median, max, nearest, idw. Each sample is an independent observation; port and starboard are never averaged together before gridding. Samples within a search radius of each cell centre contribute (radius derived from the resolution unless max_search_radius_m is given); empty cells are NaN.

Projected grids name their coordinates northing / easting (meters); geographic grids use latitude / longitude.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A UTM grid uses the zone containing the bbox centre. A survey wider than a zone puts its edges in a neighbouring zone's frame.
  • bbox_from_channel_dataset pads by a fixed amount in degrees, which is negligible for a survey but large for a very small test dataset.

docs.title: HDF5 IO
docs.text:
Read and write full :class:SideScanSurvey objects as .ss.h5 files. A single file holds all frequency channels and auxiliary records with a grouped layout that supports lazy/chunked loading.

The format is not frozen

The layout below may change in any 0.x release before 1.0, and a file written by one 0.x version may not read in a later one. Keep the raw source files and re-convert after an upgrade. The root attribute sidescanpy_version records which version wrote a file.

For single-frequency channels in standalone NetCDF, see docs/io_netcdf.md. For the schema each group conforms to, see docs/core.md.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text: Function Use case write_survey(survey, path) Write a survey to disk. read_survey(path) Read back as a validated survey. read_survey(path, chunks={"ping": N}) Lazy loading for frequency channels.

docs.title: File layout
docs.text:
survey.ss.h5
├── /                            ← root attrs: survey_name,
│                                  source_format, source_files_json,
│                                  sidescanpy_version
├── /frequencies/
│   ├── hz_547500/                ← SideScanFrequencyChannel.dataset
│   └── hz_1495000/
└── /aux_streams/
    ├── navigation/               ← always written (empty if unset)
    ├── attitude/                 ← always written (empty if unset)
    ├── dvl/                      ← always written (empty if unset)
    └── sensors/                  ← only if any sensors present
        └── pressure/

Group constants are defined in sidescanpy.core.schema (HDF5_GROUP_*) and used uniformly by reader and writer.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Engine. h5netcdf.
  • Survey metadata. Stored in root-level attrs:
  • survey_name (string)
  • source_format (string, e.g. "JSF")
  • source_files_json (JSON-encoded list of paths)
  • sidescanpy_version (the version that wrote the file; absent in files from 0.7.6 and earlier)
  • Aux records always written. A survey with no nav messages still writes an empty navigation group. This keeps the file structure consistent across surveys regardless of source content.
  • Sensors group is conditional. If a survey has zero sensors, the aux_streams/sensors/ parent group is omitted entirely. The reader handles its absence.
  • Encoding. Every frequency-channel variable with two or more dimensions is written with gzip level 4 + shuffle, chunked along ping. float64 variables are stored as float32, except latitude and longitude (float32 resolves only ~0.4 m there). Per-ping 1-D fields are uncompressed. Files from 0.5.0 that also carry backscatter_raw still read; correct_file drops that variable on rewrite.
  • Chunking on disk. HDF5_CHUNK_PING = 256 along the ping axis for frequency channel data.
  • Lazy loading. chunks={"ping": N} on read returns dask-backed arrays for frequency channel data. Aux records always load eagerly (they're tiny).

docs.title: Round-trip guarantee
docs.text:
After write_survey(survey, path); read_survey(path), the loaded survey matches the original:

  • Same frequency channels (validated as SideScanFrequencyChannel)
  • Same aux records (xr.testing.assert_identical)
  • Same survey metadata (survey_name, source_format, source_files)
  • Same processing history per channel
  • Bit-exact backscatter values, including NaN and dtype preservation

Enforced by ~57 unit tests across tests/unit/io/hdf5/test_writer.py, test_reader.py, and test_round_trip.py, plus integration tests against real JSF data.

docs.title: Performance notes
docs.text:
• For typical surveys (10k pings × 2 channels × 2000 samples), file sizes after gzip compression are roughly 30-50% of raw payload size.
  • Lazy reads with chunks={"ping": 256} align with on-disk chunks for zero-overhead access. Smaller chunk sizes work but emit a warning about misaligned reads.
  • Aux records (typically a few KB to a few MB) load eagerly and don't affect lazy-loading performance for the main backscatter arrays.

docs.title: Inspecting files manually
docs.text:
For debugging or quick inspection without loading into Python:

h5ls survey.ss.h5                   # List top-level groups
h5ls -r survey.ss.h5                # Recursive listing
h5dump -A survey.ss.h5              # Root attributes only
h5dump -H survey.ss.h5/frequencies  # Show structure of one group

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Add a multi-survey container format (multiple surveys in one file) for mosaicking workflows.
  • Consider Zarr as an alternate backend for cloud-friendly access (S3, GCS). Same xarray semantics, different storage.
  • Freeze the layout for 1.0 and add a schema_version root attribute that changes only when the layout does (sidescanpy_version records the writer, not the layout).
  • Consider compression tuning per dataset based on data characteristics (e.g. constant-valued backscatter compresses to almost nothing; noisy data benefits less).

docs.title: JSF IO
docs.text: Parses Edgetech .jsf binary survey files. Produces typed message instances and converts them into a SideScanSurvey.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text:
Function Use case read_jsf(path) Eager parse, returns full list[JSFMessage]. read_jsf_iter(path) Generator over messages — for very large files. convert(messages, source_files=...) Group + dispatch messages into a SideScanSurvey. write_subset(src, dst, n_pings=, start_ping=) Copy a run of pings to a new file, byte for byte.

The reader-converter split is intentional: the reader knows about JSF binary, the converter knows about the survey schema. Either can be swapped or tested independently.

docs.title: Message hierarchy
docs.text:
JSFMessage (base)
├── SonarDataMessage              (per-ping sidescan data)
├── PitchRollDataMessage          (attitude: roll, pitch, heave)
├── DopplerVelocityLogDataMessage (DVL: bottom dist, water vel.)
├── PressureSensorReadingMessage  (pressure, temp, sound speed)
├── NMEAStringMessage             (parent for NMEA sentences)
│   ├── NMEARMCMessage            (lat/lon/speed/course)
│   ├── NMEAGLLMessage            (lat/lon)
│   ├── NMEAGGAMessage            (lat/lon/fix quality)
│   ├── NMEAVTGMessage            (course/speed)
│   ├── NMEAZDAMessage            (date/time)
│   ├── NMEADBTMessage            (depth below transducer)
│   └── NMEADPTMessage            (depth + offset)
└── (other types: parsed but not yet routed by converter)

Each subclass implements from_bytes(header, payload) for parsing and exposes typed Python fields after __post_init__.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Timestamps. Sonar messages: timestamp_ns: int. Aux messages: timestamp: float (epoch seconds). The converter handles both via type-aware dispatch. All output time coords are datetime64[ns].
  • Invalid fields. When validity flags reject a value, current message classes use None. The converter coerces to np.nan.
  • Field naming. Schema-aligned suffixes (_deg, _m, _ms) are used on most newer fields. A few older fields still lack suffixes; see "Future work" below.

docs.title: Known device-specific issues
docs.text:
• Attitude validity flags. PitchRollDataMessage (type 2020) flags follow the spec bit layout. Devices seen so far set the pitch, roll and heading bits and clear heave and yaw, so heave_m is NaN in the attitude_record while roll, pitch and heading are populated.
  • Pressure-stuck-at-zero. PressureSensorReadingMessage has no validity gate; depth/sound_speed/temperature appear stuck at 0 in current sample data. Likely device-specific.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Unit tests use Mock(spec=...) instances. Decouples tests from binary parsing. See tests/unit/io/jsf/conftest.py.
  • tests/unit/io/test_public_fixtures.py runs on a public EdgeTech Discover JSF cut (tests/data/public/, OGL v3) and checks it against the XTF files Discover wrote for the same pings.
  • Integration tests run against a real fixture: tests/data/jsf/sample.jsf. Skipped by default; run with pytest --slow.
  • Diagnostic script: scripts/plot_jsf_aux_streams.py for evaluating source quality and overlap on a real file.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Standardize on timestamp_ns: int across all message types (currently only SonarDataMessage and PitchRollDataMessage).
  • Replace Optional[float] = None with float = nan for fields gated by validity flags. Removes the _coerce step in the converter.
  • Add a validity gate to PressureSensorReadingMessage.
  • Implement to_bytes for round-trip testing (currently NotImplementedError for most message types). Useful for synthesizing test fixtures.
  • Add NMEA types as needed: HDT (true heading), GSV (satellite info).
  • Integration test for read_jsf_iter once it's used in production.

docs.title: NetCDF IO
docs.text:
Read and write individual :class:SideScanFrequencyChannel datasets as standalone .nc files. Use this when you want to share or process a single frequency in isolation without the survey-level wrapper.

For full multi-frequency surveys with auxiliary records, see docs/io_hdf5.md.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text: Function Use case write_frequency_channel(channel, path) Write a channel to disk. read_frequency_channel(path) Read back as a validated channel. read_frequency_channel(path, chunks={"ping": N}) Lazy/dask-backed loading.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Engine. h5netcdf. Standardized across the project.
  • Encoding. The same policy as .ss.h5 (see HDF5 IO): gzip 4 + shuffle on every variable with two or more dimensions, float64 stored as float32 except latitude/longitude, per-ping fields uncompressed.
  • Chunking on disk. (chunk_ping=256, n_channels=2, n_samples=full) by default. Aligns with the dominant access pattern (per-ping reads).
  • Chunking on read. Pass chunks={"ping": N} to return dask-backed arrays. None (default) loads eagerly.
  • String coords. channel_id round-trips as native Python strings (["port", "starboard"]). The reader normalizes byte-strings if the engine returns them.

docs.title: Round-trip guarantee
docs.text:
After write_frequency_channel(ch, path); read_frequency_channel(path), the loaded dataset is xr.testing.assert_identical to the original:

  • All data values exact (including NaN preservation), except float64 variables other than latitude/longitude, which round-trip at float32 precision
  • All coords with original dtype
  • All attrs including processing_history
  • Per-ping fields and dimensions preserved

This is enforced by ~31 unit tests in tests/unit/io/netcdf/test_round_trip.py.

docs.title: Performance notes
docs.text:
• Eager read of a 50-ping × 2000-sample fixture file: <100 ms typical.
  • Lazy read with chunks={"ping": 256}: subsequent value access forces on-demand decompression of only the requested chunks.
  • For large surveys, prefer the HDF5 module — it preserves frequency channels and aux records together in one file with the same lazy loading semantics.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Verify behavior with non-default chunk sizes on read (e.g. chunks={"ping": 50} against a 256-ping on-disk chunk size). Currently works but emits a "chunks separate the stored chunks" warning.
  • Add a multi-channel NetCDF writer that bundles multiple SideScanFrequencyChannel datasets into one .nc with groups (the HDF5 writer already does this; the NetCDF version would be a convenience).

docs.title: Klein SDF format
docs.text: .sdf files are produced by Klein side-scan sonar systems (Klein 4900 and other UUV-3500-series). The format is binary, big-endian-aware, and documented in the Klein "SDF/SDFX Data Page Definitions" spec.

docs.title: File structure
docs.text:
A Klein SDF file is a sequence of pages. Each page contains:

[4 bytes: marker (always 0xFFFFFFFF)]
[512 bytes: typed header]
[variable bytes: body — sonar samples or reserved data]

Pages can be of different types, identified by page_version:

Version Description 3501 UUV-3500 Low Frequency sonar data 3502 UUV-3500 High Frequency sonar data 3000-3001 System 3000 (older) 3500 UUV-3500 (obsolete) Other Various non-sonar page types

The reader yields both sonar pages (SDFSonarPage) and non-sonar pages (SDFUnknownPage). The converter filters to sonar pages only.

docs.title: Header structure
docs.text:
The 512-byte header has 128 uint32-equivalent slots covering 100+ named fields plus 26 reserved uint32 slots. See SDFPageHeader in sidescanpy.io.sdf.pages for the full field list.

Key fields:

Field Type Notes page_size U32 Bytes from after marker to end of page page_version U32 Page type identifier ping_number U32 Increments per ping num_samples U32 Sample count per channel range_m U32 Sonar range setting (meters) speed_cms U32 Towfish speed (cm/s); use .speed_ms for m/s heading_deg, pitch_deg, roll_deg float32 Towfish attitude altitude_m float32 Altimeter reading (meters) depth_volts float32 Depth sensor (Volts; needs calibration) ship_latitude_rad, ship_longitude_rad double Ship GPS in radians fish_latitude_rad, fish_longitude_rad double Towfish position in radians sonar_freq_khz U32 Operating frequency (kHz); use .sonar_freq_hz for Hz _reserved tuple[U32; 26] Forward-compatibility slots

docs.title: Klein conventions
docs.text:
• Latitude/longitude in radians: All position fields are stored as float64 radians. Use the .ship_latitude_deg, .fish_latitude_deg etc. properties for degrees.

  • Speed in cm/s: speed_cms field is centimeters per second. Use .speed_ms for meters per second.

  • Sound speed in cm/s: Same conversion. Use .sound_speed_ms.

  • Frequency in kHz: sonar_freq_khz is kilohertz. Use .sonar_freq_hz for hertz.

  • Year handling: Older Klein firmware stores year as offset from 1900 (e.g. 126 means 2026). Newer firmware uses 4-digit years (2026). The dataclass auto-detects via _year < 200 check.

  • Time precision: Klein records hSecond (hundredths) as field 24 for backward compatibility, but fseconds (field 51) is the authoritative fractional component. The dataclass uses fseconds for timestamp computation.

docs.title: Sample data masking
docs.text:
Klein stores sample amplitudes as uint32 even though only 16 bits of amplitude are used. Bit 17 is occasionally set (~0.001% of samples in observed Klein 4900 data) as undocumented metadata.

The reader masks samples to the low 16 bits via & 0xFFFF. This removes spurious bright pixels in waterfall visualizations. Masking is logged at DEBUG level.

If you need access to the raw uint32 (including the metadata bits), use SDFPageHeader.from_bytes() and _parse_sonar_body() directly to read without masking.

docs.title: Depth sensor calibration
docs.text: The Klein depth field is stored in Volts and requires per-survey calibration data from the INI file (which we don't parse). Surveys converted from SDF have depth_m set to NaN. Users with calibration data should override the depth_m variable manually.

docs.title: Sound velocity
docs.text: Klein doesn't record sound velocity in the page header. Surveys have sound_vel_ms set to NaN. The pipeline falls back to 1500 m/s in compute_geometric_ranges.

docs.title: Aux fields with variable units
docs.text: Fields 46-49 (aux_pitch, aux_roll, aux_depth, aux_altitude) are described in the spec as "variable units" — they're carry-through fields from auxiliary sensors that may report in degrees, meters, or sensor-specific units. The dataclass exposes them as float32 values without unit conversion.

docs.title: 455 kHz channel reliability
docs.text: In one test survey, the 455 kHz transducer was non-functional; data appeared as noise floor + sparse spikes. This is a hardware condition, not a parsing issue. If you see similar patterns, check: - The transducer hardware - The error_flags field in the header for compass/sensor errors - Whether 900 kHz data shows clear seafloor returns (confirming the reader is parsing correctly)

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Klein SDF/SDFX Data Page Definitions specification
  • tests/integration/test_sdf_to_survey.py for end-to-end examples
  • scripts/batch_convert_and_plot.py for batch processing workflow

docs.title: XTF format
docs.text:
.xtf (eXtended Triton Format) is the most common vendor-neutral sidescan format: Klein, EdgeTech and others can record or export it. The reader follows the specification's revision 42 (Exail) and has been checked against EdgeTech 4200 files recorded by Isis, and against public files written by EdgeTech Discover 7.22, Isis 7.0.41 (Benthos SIS-1624) and KleinXlt 4.0 (small cuts of them are the fixtures in tests/data/public/). Only sonar packets are read; other packet types are counted and skipped.

from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert, read_and_convert_segments
from sidescanpy.io.xtf import convert, read_xtf, split_by_sample_rate

# One survey per run of constant range (see "Range changes" below):
for stem, survey in read_and_convert_segments(path):
    ...
# or, step by step:
surveys = [convert(seg) for seg in split_by_sample_rate(read_xtf(path))]

survey = read_and_convert([path], "xtf")      # whole file, one survey

read_xtf_header, iter_packets, count_packets and read_xtf_pings give the file header, the raw packets and the recorded pings (samples in their recorded dtype) for inspection. write_subset(src, dst, n_pings=, start_ping=) copies the header and a run of pings to a new file, byte for byte (for making small test files).

docs.title: File structure
docs.text: A 1024-byte file header (system, recording program, sonar name, navigation units, and one 128-byte ChanInfo per channel; more than six channels spill into further 1024-byte blocks), then packets. Every packet starts with the magic 0xFACE, a header type and its total byte count, which the reader uses to step from packet to packet. A sonar packet is a 256-byte ping header followed, per channel, by a 64-byte channel header and that channel's samples.

docs.title: Mapping to the standard model
docs.text:
Survey XTF source frequency key hz_<Hz> ChanInfo.Frequency (kHz) of a port/starboard pair backscatter_intensity (ping, channel, sample) port (TypeOfChannel 1) and starboard (2) samples, float32; sample 0 nearest the sonar on both sides (XTF stores port far -> near, so port is reversed) valid_samples per-ping NumSamples; padding beyond it is NaN latitude, longitude SensorYcoordinate, SensorXcoordinate (degrees, NavUnits 3) heading_deg, pitch_deg, roll_deg, heave_m SensorHeading, SensorPitch (nose up +), SensorRoll (port up +), Heave depth_m SensorDepth altitude_m, fathometer_reading_m SensorPrimaryAltitude; 0 is NaN sound_vel_ms SoundVelocity, doubled when below 1000 m/s (see below) sample_rate_hz NumSamples / TimeDuration time Year … Second + HSeconds (10 ms resolution) navigation / attitude records every ping header (source = extracted_from_xtf_ping_headers)

pulse_length_us is not in the XTF headers and is 0.0. Gain codes are not interpreted. Dataset attributes prefixed xtf_ record the recording program, sonar, channel numbers and names, and counts of reader anomalies.

docs.title: Conventions and caveats
docs.text:
• Sound velocity may be halved. Some recorders store c / 2 in SoundVelocity (750 for 1500 m/s). Values below 1000 m/s are doubled, and the result is cross-checked against 2 * SlantRange / TimeDuration; a disagreement over 5 % is logged at WARNING.
  • Range changes. The model has one sample_rate_hz per frequency, but some recorders change the range setting mid-file while keeping the sample count, so the sample interval changes. split_by_sample_rate cuts a file's pings into consecutive runs within which every port/starboard channel keeps its rate (NumSamples / TimeDuration, relative tolerance rtol, default 1 %, measured against the run's first ping); pings where a channel is absent never cause a cut. Runs shorter than min_pings (default 50) are dropped — a change often leaves a few pings at an intermediate setting. Each run is a view of the file's arrays and converts to its own survey, with attributes xtf_segment_index, xtf_segment_count, xtf_segment_ping_start, xtf_segment_ping_stop, xtf_file_pings, xtf_runs_dropped_short and xtf_pings_dropped_short_runs. read_and_convert_segments and sidescan-convert survey do this for every XTF file and name the outputs <stem> (one run) or <stem>_seg01, <stem>_seg02, … (several). Converting an unsplit file with mixed rates still works: the most common rate is used, the other pings are counted in xtf_pings_other_sample_rate and a WARNING is logged, since their ranges are scaled wrongly by the ratio of the rates.
  • Pings with fewer channels than declared. Some EdgeTech files begin with pings that hold only the low-frequency pair while declaring all four channels. The reader walks channel blocks by the packet byte count; those pings are left out of the high frequency (which keeps its own ping axis) and counted in xtf_pings_absent.
  • Projected coordinates (NavUnits 0) are not supported and raise NotImplementedError.

docs.title: JSF Auxiliary Stream Source Selection
docs.text:
When a JSF file is converted to a SideScanSurvey, the converter must decide which message stream populates each auxiliary record (navigation, attitude, dvl, sensors) and, separately, which stream is most accurate for interpolating per-ping values (latitude, heading_deg, etc.) at processing time.

This document describes the diagnostic methodology and the resulting decisions, so that future readers (including future-you) can audit and extend the logic without re-deriving it.

docs.title: Why this matters
docs.text:
Several physical quantities appear in multiple JSF message types. For example:

  • Latitude/longitude: carried in NMEA RMC, GLL, GGA, and embedded as a per-ping field on SonarDataMessage.
  • Roll/pitch: carried in PitchRollDataMessage, embedded on SonarDataMessage, and partially in DopplerVelocityLogDataMessage.
  • Depth: carried in PressureSensorReadingMessage, DopplerVelocityLogDataMessage, and embedded on SonarDataMessage.

These sources do not always agree. Some are direct sensor readings; others are downstream copies that lag the original by one message. Using the right source — and interpolating it correctly onto ping times — materially affects positional and attitude accuracy.

docs.title: Diagnostic methodology
docs.text:
Run the auxiliary-stream diagnostic script against a representative JSF file:

python scripts/plot_jsf_aux_streams.py path/to/file.jsf --no-plot

The script extracts every value of every quantity from every available source and prints a table with these columns per (quantity × source):

Column Meaning N Number of message arrivals N_valid Number of non-NaN values mean / std / min / max Distribution of values span_s Time span covered rate_hz Message arrival rate (N / span_s) n_changes Number of value transitions change_rate_hz Effective update rate (n_changes / span_s) hold_ms_p50 Median time the value remains constant mirror_of If the change pattern matches another source, names that source

The key distinction: arrival rate vs change rate. A source can arrive at 95 Hz but only carry new information at 0.5 Hz if 99% of its values are repeats of the previous reading.

docs.title: Mirror detection
docs.text:
When source A's change times closely match source B's arrival times, A is a mirror of B — A re-publishes B's values at A's own (faster) arrival rate. The diagnostic script computes this automatically and reports mirror_of for each (quantity, source) pair.

A typical mirror relationship: SonarDataMessage.latitude mirrors NMEARMCMessage.latitude. Sonar messages arrive at ~95 Hz; latitude within those messages updates at the NMEA rate (~0.5 Hz), one message later. The sonar's per-ping latitude is, in effect, "the most recent NMEA fix as of this ping" — useful for the embedded value but not an independent source of new information.

docs.title: Decision matrix — auxiliary records
docs.text:
This is what convert() writes to each aux record on the survey.

Aux record Source Rationale navigation NMEA RMC + GLL + GGA All three provide identical lat/lon; we collect from all three to maximize coverage. NMEA is the upstream truth for position. attitude PitchRollDataMessage Only direct source for roll/pitch/heave. Sonar embedded values mirror this stream. dvl DopplerVelocityLogDataMessage Only direct source. May be absent in some files. sensors PressureSensorReadingMessage Pressure-derived depth, water sound speed, water temperature. Currently the only supported sensor; extensible by sensor_type.

The converter does not fall back to alternate sources when the primary is empty or invalid. A field whose validity bit is clear in a PitchRollDataMessage is NaN in the attitude_record for that observation (heave on devices without a heave sensor, for example). With no attitude messages at all, the record is empty but schema-valid and the survey's has_attitude property reports False.

docs.title: Decision matrix — per-ping interpolation
docs.text:
This is the Phase 3 work. It applies after the aux records are built, when we want each (ping, *) to have an accurate latitude, heading_deg, etc. — rather than the latched-previous-fix values that sonar embedded provides.

The framework:

  1. Classify each per-ping field's sonar_embedded value as either a live sensor reading or a mirror of an aux stream, using the diagnostic script's mirror_of column.
  2. If it's a mirror, interpolate the upstream aux stream onto ping times.
  3. If it's a live sensor, leave it alone.
  4. If the upstream aux stream is empty or all-NaN, fall back to sonar_embedded with a warning.

docs.title: Per-field decisions (sample.jsf)
docs.text:
Per-ping field Sonar embedded class Interpolation source Fallback latitude mirror of NMEA NMEA aux record sonar_embedded longitude mirror of NMEA NMEA aux record sonar_embedded heading_deg mirror of attitude attitude aux record sonar_embedded roll_deg mirror of attitude attitude aux record sonar_embedded pitch_deg mirror of attitude attitude aux record sonar_embedded heave_m not in sonar attitude aux record NaN altitude_m live sensor (38 Hz) sonar_embedded DVL aux record (cross-check) depth_m live sensor (6 Hz) sonar_embedded pressure aux record (cross-check) sound_vel_ms live sensor sonar_embedded DVL or pressure water_temp_C live sensor sonar_embedded DVL or pressure course mirror of NMEA NMEA RMC/VTG sonar_embedded speed mirror of NMEA NMEA RMC/VTG sonar_embedded

These are the defaults. Different surveys may need overrides — e.g. if a particular file has bad NMEA fixes but good sonar embedded positions, the user should be able to override the source for latitude specifically.

docs.title: Worked example: sample.jsf
docs.text: Running the diagnostic on tests/data/jsf/sample.jsf produces the following key observations.

docs.title: Position is mirrored
docs.text: Latitude and longitude appear in four sources. NMEA arrives at 0.5 Hz; sonar_embedded arrives at 95 Hz. Both have effective change rates of ~0.5 Hz with hold times of ~2000 ms. Sonar embedded position is just NMEA latched. Use NMEA for interpolation.

docs.title: Attitude is mirrored
docs.text: Roll, pitch, and heading on sonar_embedded change at 10.3 Hz with 84 ms holds. PitchRollDataMessage arrives at 10 Hz. The match is exact — sonar embedded attitude is the previous attitude reading. Use attitude for interpolation.

docs.title: Altitude and depth are live
docs.text: Sonar embedded altitude updates at 38 Hz with 41 ms holds. No DVL altitude rate matches this — it's a true 38 Hz altimeter signal. Sonar embedded depth updates at 6 Hz with 166 ms holds, also a real sensor signal (likely fed by the pressure transducer at 7 Hz, but not a direct mirror). Use sonar_embedded for both.

docs.title: Sound speed and temperature are unavailable
docs.text: Stuck at 0 across all sources in this file. Either the device doesn't populate these fields, or they're behind validity flags we don't check. Survey-wide values would be required from external metadata (CTD cast, climatology). Per-ping values stay at 0 / NaN until a real source is identified.

docs.title: Attitude validity flags
docs.text: PitchRollDataMessage.parse_validity_flags() follows the spec bit layout. On the devices seen so far, pitch, roll and heading bits are set and heave and yaw bits are clear, so heave_m is NaN.

docs.title: Timing vs value alignment
docs.text:
The mirror_of column identifies sources whose change timing aligns with another source's arrival times. It does not verify that the values agree.

In sample.jsf, for example, the diagnostic reports:

depth sonar_embedded → mirror_of: pressure

But pressure depth is stuck at 0 across the file, while sonar_embedded depth ranges from 3.5 to 6.0 m. The timing alignment is real — sonar embedded depth happens to update at the same cadence pressure messages arrive — but the values come from a different sensor entirely (the sonar's internal depth fix, embedded into the ping message).

When choosing an interpolation source: 1. Check mirror_of for the timing relationship. 2. Cross-check mean and std between the candidate sources to confirm they agree on values. 3. If timing matches but values diverge, the apparent mirror is a coincidence of update cadence, not a real upstream source.

docs.title: Pressure sensor stuck at 0
docs.text:
PressureSensorReadingMessage has no validity flag check (unlike sonar/attitude/DVL). If the device doesn't populate a field, it arrives as 0 and is treated as a valid reading. Currently affects:

  • depth_m
  • sound_speed_ms
  • temperature_C

Investigate whether the device intends 0 as "not provided" and add a validity gate accordingly.

See TODO in sidescanpy/io/jsf/messages.py.

docs.title: Extending this analysis to new files
docs.text:
For each new survey or new device:

  1. Run python scripts/plot_jsf_aux_streams.py <file.jsf> --no-plot.
  2. For each quantity, check the change_rate_hz and mirror_of columns.
  3. If a sonar_embedded row reports mirror_of: <other_source>, use that other source as the interpolation seed.
  4. If change_rate_hz significantly exceeds any aux source's rate_hz, sonar_embedded is the live sensor — use it directly.
  5. Update the per-field decisions table above if the file changes the default selections.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• JSF format spec: Edgetech 2.x JSF File Format Specification
  • sidescanpy/io/jsf/messages.py — message parsing
  • sidescanpy/io/jsf/converter.py — _build_*_record functions
  • scripts/plot_jsf_aux_streams.py — diagnostic script

Last revised 2026 by rshomberg@uri.edu.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The library logs through logging.getLogger("sidescanpy.<module>") and never configures handlers itself:

  • DEBUG: routine progress and decisions (a skipped step, a masked region, per-file progress).
  • WARNING: something about the data the caller should know (missing sound velocity, an empty aux stream, a target that could not be matched).
  • Library code never logs at INFO and never prints.

In a script:

from sidescanpy.log import configure_logging, log_timing

configure_logging("INFO")          # or "DEBUG" to see library detail
with log_timing("correct survey"):
    ...

configure_logging is idempotent and keeps noisy third-party loggers at WARNING. The CLI commands set it up from -v, -q and --log-file.

docs.title: Pre-release status
docs.text: sidescanpy's code is shared by invitation before its public release; this documentation is public. This page covers what that means for you: what may still change, how to get access and install it, where the test data is, and how to report problems.

docs.title: What may change before 1.0
docs.text:
Until version 1.0, any 0.x release can change:

  • The .ss.h5 file format. Group layout, variable names, attributes and encodings are not frozen. A file written by one 0.x version may not read, or may read differently, in a later one. There is no migration tool yet.
  • The Python API and the CLI. Functions, parameters, defaults, flags and config keys can be renamed or removed.
  • Default processing parameters, such as the TVG spreading term, and so the numbers a default correct_survey run produces.

Breaking changes are listed in CHANGELOG.md under the release that makes them.

To protect your own work:

  • Keep the raw JSF, SDF and XTF files. They are the archive. Treat .ss.h5 files as derived products you can regenerate, and expect to re-convert after an upgrade.
  • Pin the version your project uses (a tag or a commit, see below), and upgrade on purpose.
  • Check which version wrote a file. Each .ss.h5 records the writer in the root attribute sidescanpy_version (files from 0.7.6 and earlier lack it), and every processing step records its version in processing_history:
import h5netcdf

with h5netcdf.File("survey.ss.h5", "r") as f:
    print(f.attrs.get("sidescanpy_version", "0.7.6 or earlier"))

docs.title: Access
docs.text: The repository is private. Invited people get read access: you can clone it, install from it and open issues. Please don't pass the code or the test data link on outside your group before the public release; ask instead, and access can be added. This site and the example data are public and can be shared freely.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
sidescanpy is not on PyPI yet. Install it from the repository, pinned to a release tag (or main for the latest fixes), with an SSH key or a gh auth login session that GitHub accepts for your account:

uv pip install "sidescanpy[viz] @ git+ssh://git@github.com/rshomberg-research/sidescanpy.git@v0.7.6"
# or over HTTPS
uv pip install "sidescanpy[viz] @ git+https://github.com/rshomberg-research/sidescanpy.git@main"

In a uv project, uv add "sidescanpy[viz] @ git+ssh://git@github.com/rshomberg-research/sidescanpy.git@v0.7.6" records the pin in pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The extras are listed in the README.

To work on the code itself, clone it and run uv sync --all-extras.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: This site, https://rshomberg-research.github.io/sidescanpy/, follows main. For the docs of a release tag, or offline, either build them from a clone (make docs-serve, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000) or download the sidescanpy-docs artifact of that tag's docs run from the repository's Actions tab (kept 90 days).

docs.title: Test and example data
docs.text:
The repository holds code only, no survey data.

  • Test fixtures. Five small cuts (4.1 MB) of openly licensed public recordings: EdgeTech JSF, and XTF from three writers. Their sources, licences and checksums are in tests/data/public/SOURCES.md. They come as one zip, shared by link with invited people. Unzip it and point SIDESCANPY_PUBLIC_DATA at the folder:

    export SIDESCANPY_PUBLIC_DATA=/path/to/sidescanpy-public-fixtures
uv run pytest tests/unit/io/test_public_fixtures.py

    Without the variable those tests skip. The fixtures are also handy as small real files to try the readers on.

  • Examples. The worked examples download public recordings with sidescanpy.datasets.fetch(), which needs no access to anything private. The other scripts in examples/ run on synthetic data. An archived copy of the example data with a DOI is planned for the public release.

Data you get from us keeps its original licence (UK Open Government Licence v3, or U.S. public domain); credit the sources as SOURCES.md asks.

docs.title: Feedback
docs.text: Open an issue on GitHub. For a reader problem, say which sonar and acquisition software wrote the file and attach the shortest file that shows it, or a cut made with io.jsf.write_subset / io.xtf.write_subset, if you can share it.

docs.title: Processing
docs.text: sidescanpy.processing corrects, slices and measures frequency-channel datasets. Every function takes and returns an xr.Dataset; the input is never modified.

docs.title: Corrections
docs.text:
One API applies an ordered list of steps:

Function Applies steps to correct(ds, steps, params, aux=None, force=False) one frequency channel correct_survey(survey, steps, params, force=False) every channel of a survey (feeds the survey's navigation/attitude records to interpolate_aux) correct_file(path, steps, params, out_path=None, chunk_pings=None) a .ss.h5 file, written atomically (in place by default), optionally in ping chunks to bound memory 
from sidescanpy.processing import correct

ds = correct(ds, ["tvg", "geometric"], params={"tvg": {"spreading_loss_db": 30.0}})

docs.title: Built-in steps
docs.text:
In canonical order. DEFAULT_STEPS is interpolate_aux → tvg → geometric → georef.

Step Function Parameters crop_farrange crop_far_range cutoff_sample, n_bins, min_valid_fraction, rise_threshold_db, margin_bins interpolate_aux interpolate_aux_onto_dataset fields, method, extrapolation, drop_invalid, held_values, max_hold_s, per_ping_fallback, groups, merge_window_s bottom_track altitude_from_bottom_track replace, max_diff_m, min_altitude_m, min_return_m, min_return_fraction, smooth_window, threshold_fraction, min_run, smooth_pings tvg apply_tvg spreading_loss_db, absorption_db_per_m, min_range_m, sound_velocity_ms, temperature_c, salinity_psu, depth_m, ph geometric compute_geometric_ranges expose_unmasked_z range_correction apply_empirical_range_correction table (required) georef compute_georeferencing ellipsoid

Steps run in the order given; respecting dependencies is the caller's job (georef and range_correction need geometric; bottom_track must run before geometric to affect it). bottom_track is not in DEFAULT_STEPS.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Skip a step by leaving it out. params may only name steps that are in steps; a typo raises ValueError, and an unknown parameter raises TypeError. Both are checked before anything runs.
  • Custom steps. Any callable fn(ds, **params) -> ds, or Step(name, fn), can be a step. It is recorded in history like a built-in. Give each one a distinct name; lambdas are rejected.
  • Idempotent. A step already recorded in processing_history is skipped, so re-running is a no-op. force=True re-applies it; a radiometric step is inverted first, so new parameters replace the old ones instead of stacking.
  • History. Each applied step appends {"step", "params", "function", "version", "timestamp_utc"} with the parameters actually used.
  • No raw copy. Corrections modify backscatter_intensity in place. invert(ds) undoes recorded steps, and uncorrected_backscatter(ds) returns the signal with every radiometric step undone. processing_level(ds) reports the latest applied level (raw, tvg, geometric, range_correction, georef).

docs.title: TVG
docs.text:
apply_tvg adds the two-way propagation loss back:

  • Spreading: spreading_loss_db * log10(R). The default, 30, models the insonified seafloor patch growing in proportion to range: two-way spherical spreading (40) less 10 log R (e.g. J. Mar. Sci. Eng. 2017, 5(4), 54). Which fits real data varies; measure it per survey with analysis.fit_range_decay (pass the same spreading_loss_db) and set the coefficient in the config. 40 was the default in 0.7.0-0.7.5 and 20 (one-way spreading) before 0.7.0; files corrected with either record the value in their history, so invert() still undoes them exactly.
  • Absorption: 2 * alpha * R. When absorption_db_per_m is not given, alpha comes from the Francois-Garrison model for the channel's frequency (francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m), using temperature_c, salinity_psu, depth_m and ph (defaults 10 °C, 35 psu, 10 m, pH 8). The resolved value is recorded in history.

Linear amplitude is converted to dB as 20 * log10(clip(x, 1e-6)) first, so exact zeros map to about -120 dB. A zero or missing sound velocity falls back to 1500 m/s. Setting a term to 0 turns it off, which is how to avoid correcting a loss the hardware already compensated.

References:

  • R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part I: Pure water and magnesium sulfate contributions," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(3), 896-907 (1982).
  • R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part II: Boric acid contribution and equation for total absorption," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(6), 1879-1890 (1982).

docs.title: Geometric ranges
docs.text:
compute_geometric_ranges adds per-sample slant_range_m, ground_range_m, across_track_m (port negative, starboard positive, pitch-corrected) and related variables:

  • Slant range: sample * sound_vel / (2 * sample_rate), from the absolute sample coordinate, so a dataset trimmed of leading samples keeps its true ranges.
  • Ground range (flat bottom): sqrt(slant² - altitude²) where slant > altitude, NaN in the water column. A ping with NaN altitude gets NaN ground range (and no georeferenced position); altitude 0 gives ground range equal to slant range. Both are logged at WARNING.

docs.title: Altitude from the bottom track
docs.text:
Some recordings have no usable altitude: no altimeter, no bottom lock, or a recorder that writes 0. altitude_from_bottom_track (the bottom_track step) measures it from the data: the onset of the bottom return on each channel (detect_first_bottom_return on the uncorrected amplitude, refined to the half-rise sample), the nearer channel, in metres of slant range. By default it fills only pings whose altitude_m is NaN or <= 0; max_diff_m also replaces recorded values that disagree with the track by more than that (a lost lock that still writes a value), and replace="all" replaces every ping.

The return must stay above threshold for min_return_m (default 5 m) of slant range, of which min_return_fraction (default 70 %) must be above: a transmit burst lasts a metre or two, a seabed return tens of metres, and the fraction lets shadows in a rough seabed through. On public test files with a recorded altimeter (Benthos SIS-1624, about 30 m altitude) the tracked value agreed to within 0.2 m for 90 % of pings. The first return comes from the beam's near edge, so on sloping or very shallow seabed the tracked value is the slant range to the nearest bottom point, a little above the true altitude (+0.6 m at 1.7 m altitude on a Klein 3000 file).

docs.title: Georeferencing
docs.text: compute_georeferencing adds latitude_per_sample and longitude_per_sample from the per-ping position, heading and across-track offset on the WGS84 ellipsoid.

docs.title: Navigation interpolation
docs.text:
interpolate_aux_onto_pings (and the interpolate_aux step) replaces per-ping latitude, longitude, heading, roll, pitch and heave with values interpolated from the survey's navigation and attitude records (DEFAULT_FIELD_SOURCES). Altitude, depth and sound velocity are live sensor readings and are not interpolated by default; see JSF aux source selection. interpolate_onto_channel takes any external xr.Dataset with a time coordinate, such as a separate GPS log.

Sample-and-hold aux streams. Recorders commonly log the latest GPS fix or attitude value at every ping or packet, so a value repeats until the sensor updates (a ~1 Hz GPS under ~10 Hz pings repeats each position about ten times; attitude streams repeat on their own schedules). Interpolating those entries as logged keeps the stair-steps: consecutive pings stack on one position, then jump, which shows up in ground-range and georeferenced output. By default (held_values="fixes") each aux record is first reduced with held_value_fixes:

  • every variable is its own group, latitude and longitude included, since some recorders log the two coordinates of one fix in separate entries (groups=[POSITION_GROUP] joins them);
  • an entry is a fix when its group's value differs from the previous finite entry; NaN entries are never fixes;
  • a fix that ends a held run is placed midway between the last held entry and the changed one (the update arrived in between); a fix right after another fix keeps its own time, so a stream with no repeats is unchanged;
  • duplicate timestamps collapse to the last entry logged at that time;
  • a value held for longer than max_hold_s (default 2 s) also keeps an anchor at its last entry, so the track stays flat across a real stop or a sensor dropout instead of ramping through it.

Some recorders also spread one sensor update over consecutive entries: the bulk change, then a small follow-up (a few cm) one entry later, then nothing until the next update. Every change then becomes a fix, two fixes land one entry apart, and the interpolated speed swings between a fraction of and several times the true speed. merge_window_s (default None, no merging) collapses changes of one group that are at most that many seconds apart (chained) into one update event:

  • the event carries the group's value after its last change;
  • it is timed like a fix at its first change (the midpoint after a hold): the update started reaching the log there, and the follow-ups complete it rather than report new motion. This gives every event the same latency, whereas timing at the last change would add a delay that depends on how many entries the update spread over;
  • a max_hold_s hold is measured from the event's last change;
  • groups merge independently, and the record's first entry is never merged.

Choose the window longer than the follow-up delay (one entry) and shorter than the gap from the follow-up to the next update; about two log intervals usually fits. Too long a window chains successive updates into one event and is far worse than no merging. A float applies to every group of every record, so a window sized for a ~3 Hz GPS also chains the changes of a ~10 Hz roll sensor; a mapping by variable name, such as merge_window_s={"latitude": 0.15, "longitude": 0.15}, merges only the groups holding those variables (a group takes the smallest window of its variables). A WARNING is logged when an event combines more than five changes. aux_update_events(record, groups=..., merge_window_s=...) reports, per group, the entries, raw changes, events after merging, the percentiles (p5–p95) of the gaps between changes and between events, in entries and seconds, and the fraction of changes that fall within the window of the previous one. Split updates show as bimodal change gaps (a peak at 1 entry and one at the update interval) that become unimodal event gaps once merged. On a line running mostly north–south one coordinate barely changes, so per-coordinate change counts say little about how updates are split; check the joint group (groups=[POSITION_GROUP]) too.

The step's groups parameter is passed to held_value_fixes for each record, applying a group only where all its variables exist, so groups=[POSITION_GROUP] joins latitude and longitude in the navigation record and leaves attitude alone.

When a field has no usable aux source (record absent or empty, variable missing or all NaN), per_ping_fallback=True (default) reduces the channel's own per-ping values the same way and interpolates those. The step's history record carries held_values, max_hold_s, per_ping_fallback, per_ping_fallback_fields, groups and merge_window_s. held_values="raw" interpolates the entries as logged, as in 0.7.2 and earlier.

The step is skipped on files whose history already records it; re-convert, or correct with force=True, to apply the reduction to a file corrected before.

docs.title: Slicing
docs.text:
Function Keeps slice_by_pings(ds, start=, stop=) a ping index range slice_by_samples(ds, start=, stop=) a range of the absolute sample coordinate slice_by_range(ds, min_m, max_m) samples within a slant-range window slice_by_ground_range(ds, range_max_m=) samples within a ground range (needs geometric) slice_by_time(ds, start=, stop=) a time window slice_by_bbox(ds, lat_min=, lat_max=, lon_min=, lon_max=) pings (or, with use_per_sample=True, samples) inside a lat/lon box slice_survey(survey, fn, **kwargs) applies any slicer to every frequency of a survey

Slicing keeps processing_history.

docs.title: Bottom, nadir and noise
docs.text: Function What it does detect_first_bottom_return per-(ping, channel) sample where the bottom echo starts altitude_from_bottom_track altitude_m from the first bottom return (the bottom_track step) mask_nadir_gap NaN everything before the first bottom return detect_nadir_noise_extent, blank_nadir_noise find and zero an electronic noise burst at nadir smooth_boundary_across_pings rolling median of a per-ping boundary crop_far_range, detect_far_range_cutoff_sample find and crop far-range noise that rises above the floor reject_range_outliers per-range-bin median/MAD outlier rejection mask_bright_ping_rows mask pings much brighter than their neighbours

docs.title: Segments
docs.text: find_segments splits a file into contiguous segments and labels each one clean or excluded, from gaps in time or position (detect_gaps), hardware setting changes (detect_setting_changes), dropout or garbage runs (detect_garbage_runs) and attitude instability (detect_unstable_spans). split_by_segments returns one sub-survey per clean segment, and write_segments writes each clean segment to its own <label>.ss.h5.

docs.title: Profiles and tracks
docs.text:
• backscatter_vs_range / backscatter_vs_sample: per-bin mean, median, std, percentiles and count.
  • along_track_distance_m(ds, fill_nav_stalls=False): cumulative geodesic distance along the track; fill_nav_stalls spreads pings that repeat a navigation fix.
  • build_survey_track(surveys, freq_key, scanline_stride=): nadir track and strided scan-line endpoints as a SurveyTrack.

docs.title: Visualization
docs.text: sidescanpy.viz draws one result per call and returns matplotlib Axes / Figure; nothing is saved. Requires the [viz] extra.

docs.title: Waterfalls, grids and tracks
docs.text:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sidescanpy.viz import plot_waterfall

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6))
plot_waterfall(ds, x_axis="across_track", y_axis="along_track", ax=ax, show_colorbar=True)
fig.savefig("waterfall.png")
x_axis Meaning Needs sample (default) sample index, port mirrored nothing ground_range across-bottom distance, signed by side geometric across_track signed across-track distance, pitch-corrected geometric y_axis Meaning ping (default) ping number (ping_offset keeps survey-wide numbering for a slice) time ping timestamp along_track cumulative geodesic distance

Colour limits default to the 1st–99th percentile of finite values (vmin_pct / vmax_pct, or fixed vmin / vmax); gamma applies a power-law display stretch without changing the colorbar's units. The default colormap is copper; NaN cells render in a neutral colour.

Also: plot_survey_overview (whole survey compressed), plot_gridded_raster, plot_track_and_scanlines, plot_track_with_targets, plot_target_position_scatter, contact_sheet, render_target_context. Basemaps behind georeferenced plots need the [maps] extra.

docs.title: Analysis plots
docs.text:
One per analysis result: plot_value_histograms, plot_units_distribution, plot_sample_ping, plot_outlier_comparison, plot_cross_track_profile, plot_nadir_zoom, plot_nadir_waterfall, plot_beam_geometry, plot_usable_range, plot_segments_overview, plot_navigation_summary, plot_mean_vs_range, plot_tvg_gain_curve, plot_per_ping_profiles, plot_multi_frequency_comparison, plot_altitude_bin_comparison, plot_candidate_fit, plot_range_decay_fit, plot_range_decay_residuals, set_fit_window_limits.

Multi-panel figure layouts are in examples/figures/.

docs.title: Building a processing workflow
docs.text: sidescanpy is a library: it converts, corrects, grids and exports, but it does not decide what your survey needs. That decision is made by looking at the data, so the workflow lives in your own project, as scripts or notebooks that call the library. This page describes a layout that works well for real surveys, and the template in examples/project_template/ implements it.

docs.title: One script per step
docs.text:
01_convert.py   raw .jsf/.sdf/.xtf -> .ss.h5, target catalog -> targets.json
02_analyze.py   measure the uncorrected data (usable range, TVG decay)
03_correct.py   apply the corrections chosen from step 2
04_export.py    waterfalls, track, grids, GeoTIFF
05_dataset.py   COCO/YOLO training dataset

Run them one at a time. Several steps take a long time on real data, and each one's output decides the next one's settings: the decay fit in step 2 tells you which TVG terms to apply in step 3; the corrected overview from step 3 tells you whether the export settings in step 4 make sense. A single "run everything" driver hides exactly the moments you need to look.

Each step:

  • reads the same survey config (config.yaml);
  • writes its outputs under one output root, in its own folder;
  • writes QA figures next to them;
  • writes a report (reports/<step>.md and .json) with the numbers it measured, the figures to look at, anything that needs checking, and the command for the next step;
  • logs to the console and to logs/<step>_<timestamp>.log.

docs.title: One config per survey
docs.text:
Everything survey-specific lives in one YAML file: input and output paths, the frequencies to process, the TVG recipe, export settings and the dataset spec. A second survey gets its own copy, and nothing in the scripts changes.

correct:
  steps: [tvg, geometric, georef]
  chunk_pings: 2000
  params:
    tvg: {spreading_loss_db: 30.0}
  frequency_params:            # per-frequency overrides
    hz_1495000: {tvg: {absorption_db_per_m: 0.2}}
    hz_547500:  {tvg: {absorption_db_per_m: 0.1}}

dataset:                       # a DatasetSpec; unknown keys are an error
  styles: [chip, dual-swath]
  render_level: geometric
  size_px: 300

Recipes do not transfer between surveys, even from the same sonar. Run the analysis step on every new survey and check its report before correcting.

docs.title: What the library gives each step
docs.text: Step Library calls convert io.read_and_convert, processing.crop_far_range_noise, io.hdf5.write_survey, io.read_target_catalog, targets.correlate (Klein positions by time) analyze analysis.estimate_usable_range, analysis.fit_range_decay, processing.invert (to analyze already-corrected files) correct processing.correction_steps, processing.correct_file(..., frequency_params=, chunk_pings=) export io.hdf5.concat_survey_frequency, processing.ping_windows, targets.correlate.correlate_catalog, targets.waterfall.waterfall_boxes, grids.grid_channel, grids.to_geotiff, viz.* dataset export.ml.DatasetSpec, export.ml.build_target_dataset

docs.title: Iterating
docs.text:
Corrections are recorded in each file's processing_history and skipped when already applied, so re-running step 3 only does what is missing. To change a recipe, re-correct with force=True: radiometric steps are inverted from their recorded parameters first, so new parameters replace the old ones instead of stacking. processing.invert(ds) gives the uncorrected signal back at any time; no raw copy is stored.

For work the steps don't cover (cutting out a bad stretch, a different nadir mask, your own gain curve), pass your own function as a step:

from sidescanpy.processing import Step, correct

def drop_near_range(ds, max_sample=50):
    return ds.isel(sample=slice(max_sample, None))

ds = correct(ds, [Step("drop_near_range", drop_near_range), "tvg"],
             params={"drop_near_range": {"max_sample": 80}})

It is recorded in history like a built-in step.

docs.title: Notebooks
docs.text: The same calls work interactively. A notebook is a good place to decide a recipe; the step scripts are a good place to apply it to a whole survey once decided, repeatably.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Each example runs sidescanpy on a real, openly licensed recording that anyone can download, and shows the code and the image it makes. The code on each page is the script in examples/gallery/, included as is.

Example What it shows Data Read a file Convert a raw JSF file, save .ss.h5, plot the waterfall JNCC Wight-Barfleur, EdgeTech Correct a line Altitude from the bottom track, TVG, slant to ground range JNCC Wight-Barfleur, EdgeTech Grid to a map Gridding to UTM, GeoTIFF output JNCC mid-Irish Sea, Benthos Three formats, one model The same calls on EdgeTech JSF, Benthos XTF and Klein XTF JNCC and USGS

docs.title: Running them
docs.text:
python examples/gallery/correct_a_line.py out/

Each script writes its figure to the directory you give it (the current one by default). make gallery runs them all and refreshes the images on these pages. Plotting needs the viz extra and the GeoTIFF in Grid to a map the geo extra.

docs.title: The example data
docs.text:
sidescanpy.datasets.fetch(name) returns a local path to a recording, downloading it the first time. Each recording is one file inside a large public agency archive (8 to 57 GB); fetch reads just that file out of the archive with HTTP range requests, checks its SHA-256 and caches it.

from sidescanpy import datasets

datasets.list_datasets()          # the names fetch() accepts
path = datasets.fetch("usgs_grand_bay_150602205800.xtf")
print(datasets.citation("usgs_grand_bay_150602205800.xtf"))

Files are cached in ~/.cache/sidescanpy, or in SIDESCANPY_DATA_DIR when set. A file already there with the right checksum is used without going online.

Name Size Recording jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf 40 MB EdgeTech JSF (Discover), 219 + 521 kHz, no recorded altitude jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522H.xtf 27 MB The same pings, high frequency, as XTF (Discover 7.22) jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522L.xtf 13 MB The same pings, low frequency, as XTF (Discover 7.22) jncc_mid_irish_sea_MIS11_0.xtf 41 MB Benthos SIS-1624, XTF (Isis 7.0.41), 100 + 400 kHz jncc_mid_irish_sea_MIS13_2.xtf 4 MB The same sonar, a short line usgs_grand_bay_150602205800.xtf 5 MB Klein, XTF (KleinXlt 4.0 / SonarPro 12), shallow estuary usgs_grand_bay_150531200100.xtf 12 MB Klein, XTF; the recorded altitude is a lost bottom track

docs.title: Correct a line
docs.text:
correct_survey applies an ordered list of correction steps. Each step is optional, can be replaced by your own function, and is recorded with its parameters in the dataset's processing_history, so a corrected file says how it was made.

This JNCC line records no altitude above the seabed, which the slant-to-ground-range step needs. The bottom_track step picks it from the first seabed return in each ping (17.5 m here) before geometric runs.

Left: raw amplitude against slant range. Right: after the bottom track, time-varying gain (spreading and absorption losses) and slant-to-ground range, against across-track and along-track distance in metres. The water column is gone, and the far range is no longer darker than the near range.

"""
Correct a line: altitude from the bottom track, TVG, slant to ground range.

The JNCC Wight-Barfleur EdgeTech line records no altitude, so the
``bottom_track`` step picks it from the first seabed return before the
geometric step needs it. The figure shows the 521 kHz channel raw (slant
range) and corrected (ground range, along-track metres).

Usage:
    python examples/gallery/correct_a_line.py [output_dir]

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sidescanpy import datasets
from sidescanpy.core.units import linear_to_db
from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert
from sidescanpy.log import configure_logging
from sidescanpy.processing import compute_geometric_ranges, correct_survey, slice_by_range
from sidescanpy.viz import plot_waterfall

out = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(".")
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
configure_logging("INFO")

survey = read_and_convert([datasets.fetch("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf")], fmt="jsf")
raw = compute_geometric_ranges(survey.get_frequency("hz_521000").dataset.copy(deep=True))
raw = slice_by_range(raw, max_m=150)

# Each step is optional and recorded in processing_history with its
# parameters. Leave a step out to skip it, or pass your own function.
survey = correct_survey(
    survey,
    steps=["interpolate_aux", "bottom_track", "tvg", "geometric", "georef"],
)
corrected = slice_by_range(survey.get_frequency("hz_521000").dataset, max_m=150)
print(f"altitude from bottom track: {float(corrected['altitude_m'].median()):.1f} m (median)")

fig, (ax_raw, ax_cor) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), constrained_layout=True)
plot_waterfall(raw, x_axis="slant_range", gamma=0.5, ax=ax_raw, title="Raw (slant range)")
# Look at the corrected intensities in dB. After TVG most of the seabed
# sits within a few dB, so stretch the colour scale over the 10th to
# 99.5th percentile.
corrected = corrected.assign(backscatter_db=linear_to_db(corrected["backscatter_intensity"]))
plot_waterfall(corrected, x_axis="across_track", y_axis="along_track", value_var="backscatter_db",
               vmin_pct=10, vmax_pct=99.5, ax=ax_cor, title="Bottom track + TVG + ground range (dB)")
fig.savefig(out / "correct_a_line.png", dpi=110)

The default TVG uses 30 log R spreading and Francois-Garrison absorption. Whether a sonar already applied some gain in hardware varies; analysis.fit_range_decay measures what a dataset still needs (see examples/tvg_calibration.py).

Data: JNCC Wight-Barfleur Reef, Open Government Licence v3.0 (see the example data).

docs.title: Grid to a map
docs.text:
Once every sample has a latitude and longitude (the georef step), grid_channel resamples a channel onto a regular UTM grid and to_geotiff writes it for a GIS.

One line of a Benthos SIS-1624 survey in the Irish Sea, 100 kHz and 400 kHz, on 1 m grids. North is up; the dark stripe is the nadir under the towfish.

"""
Grid a corrected line onto a UTM map and write a GeoTIFF.

Uses a Benthos SIS-1624 line (XTF written by Isis) from the UK JNCC
mid-Irish Sea survey, which records altitude and navigation, so the
default correction steps are enough. Needs the ``geo`` extra for the
GeoTIFF.

Usage:
    python examples/gallery/grid_to_a_map.py [output_dir]

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sidescanpy import datasets
from sidescanpy.grids import grid_channel, to_geotiff
from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert
from sidescanpy.log import configure_logging
from sidescanpy.processing import correct_survey, slice_by_range
from sidescanpy.viz import plot_gridded_raster

out = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(".")
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
configure_logging("INFO")

survey = read_and_convert([datasets.fetch("jncc_mid_irish_sea_MIS11_0.xtf")], fmt="xtf")
survey = correct_survey(survey)  # interpolate_aux, tvg, geometric, georef

# Grid each frequency at 1 m, leaving out the water column. Pings are
# about 0.65 m apart, but heading jitter and a few longer jumps between
# fixes leave empty cells; inverse-distance weighting with a 4 m search
# radius fills them from the nearest samples.
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 7), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, freq_key in zip(axes, ["hz_100000", "hz_400000"]):
    ds = slice_by_range(survey.get_frequency(freq_key).dataset, min_m=5)
    raster = grid_channel(ds, resolution_m=1.0, method="idw", max_search_radius_m=4.0)
    to_geotiff(raster, out / f"mid_irish_sea_{freq_key}.tif")
    plot_gridded_raster(raster, fig=fig, ax=ax, cmap="copper", vmin_pct=2, vmax_pct=98,
                        title=f"{freq_key}, 1 m UTM grid")
fig.savefig(out / "grid_to_a_map.png", dpi=110)

Navigation in this file is sample-and-hold: each position repeats for several pings until the next fix arrives. The interpolate_aux step interpolates between the real fixes, not the repeated entries, which puts the pings about 0.65 m apart. The GeoTIFF needs the geo extra (rioxarray).

Data: JNCC mid-Irish Sea, Open Government Licence v3.0 (see the example data).

docs.title: Read a file
docs.text:
Convert one raw EdgeTech JSF line to sidescanpy's data model, save it as .ss.h5, and look at it. read_and_convert reads JSF, Klein SDF and XTF into the same structure: a SideScanSurvey holding one xarray.Dataset per frequency, with backscatter shaped (ping, channel, sample) (channel 0 is port, 1 starboard) plus the navigation and attitude records.

The two frequencies of the same 288 pings, raw amplitude against slant range. The dark band in the middle is the water column under the towfish; the seabed starts where it ends, about 18 m out on each side. A linear seabed feature runs along the starboard side at about 50 m.

"""
Read a raw sonar file and look at it.

Downloads one EdgeTech JSF line (40 MB) from the UK JNCC Wight-Barfleur
Reef survey, converts it to sidescanpy's data model, saves it as .ss.h5,
and plots the raw waterfall of both frequencies.

Usage:
    python examples/gallery/read_a_file.py [output_dir]

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from sidescanpy import datasets
from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert
from sidescanpy.io.hdf5 import write_survey
from sidescanpy.log import configure_logging
from sidescanpy.processing import compute_geometric_ranges
from sidescanpy.viz import plot_waterfall

out = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(".")
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
configure_logging("INFO")

# Download (once) and convert. read_and_convert takes JSF, SDF or XTF.
path = datasets.fetch("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf")
survey = read_and_convert([path], fmt="jsf")
write_survey(survey, out / "wight_barfleur.ss.h5", overwrite=True)

# One xarray Dataset per frequency: backscatter is (ping, channel, sample),
# channel 0 = port, 1 = starboard.
for freq_key in sorted(survey.frequencies):
    ds = survey.get_frequency(freq_key).dataset
    print(freq_key, dict(ds.sizes))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 5), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, freq_key in zip(axes, sorted(survey.frequencies)):
    ds = compute_geometric_ranges(survey.get_frequency(freq_key).dataset)
    plot_waterfall(ds, x_axis="slant_range", gamma=0.5, ax=ax,
                   title=f"{freq_key}: raw, slant range")
fig.savefig(out / "read_a_file.png", dpi=110)

It prints the size of each frequency:

hz_218740 {'ping': 287, 'channel': 2, 'sample': 11568}
hz_521000 {'ping': 288, 'channel': 2, 'sample': 23140}

The reader also logs two warnings worth knowing about: this file records no sound velocity (1500 m/s is used) and no altitude. Correct a line fills the altitude in.

Data: JNCC Wight-Barfleur Reef, Open Government Licence v3.0 (see the example data).

docs.title: Three formats, one model
docs.text:
Three sonars, three file formats or writers, the same code. Each line is read with read_and_convert, TVG-corrected with correct_survey and plotted with plot_waterfall; only the file name and format string change.

From left: EdgeTech (JSF written by Discover), Benthos SIS-1624 (XTF written by Isis) and Klein (XTF written by SonarPro), each in dB against slant range.

"""
One data model, any format: the same code on three sonars and writers.

EdgeTech JSF (Discover), Benthos XTF (Isis) and Klein XTF (SonarPro),
each read, TVG-corrected and plotted with identical calls. The JNCC line
was also written by Discover as XTF; both readers return the same samples.

Usage:
    python examples/gallery/three_formats.py [output_dir]

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu
"""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from sidescanpy import datasets
from sidescanpy.core.units import linear_to_db
from sidescanpy.io import read_and_convert
from sidescanpy.log import configure_logging
from sidescanpy.processing import compute_geometric_ranges, correct_survey
from sidescanpy.viz import plot_waterfall

out = Path(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else Path(".")
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
configure_logging("INFO")

lines = [
    ("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf", "jsf", "hz_218740", "EdgeTech JSF (Discover)"),
    ("jncc_mid_irish_sea_MIS11_0.xtf", "xtf", "hz_100000", "Benthos XTF (Isis)"),
    ("usgs_grand_bay_150602205800.xtf", "xtf", "hz_100000", "Klein XTF (SonarPro)"),
]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 5), constrained_layout=True)
for ax, (name, fmt, freq_key, label) in zip(axes, lines):
    survey = read_and_convert([datasets.fetch(name)], fmt=fmt)
    survey = correct_survey(survey, steps=["tvg"])
    ds = compute_geometric_ranges(survey.get_frequency(freq_key).dataset)
    ds = ds.assign(backscatter_db=linear_to_db(ds["backscatter_intensity"]))
    plot_waterfall(ds, x_axis="slant_range", value_var="backscatter_db",
                   vmin_pct=10, vmax_pct=99.5, ax=ax, title=f"{label}, {freq_key}")
fig.savefig(out / "three_formats.png", dpi=110)

# The same pings, written by EdgeTech Discover once as JSF and once as XTF.
jsf = read_and_convert([datasets.fetch("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf")], fmt="jsf")
xtf = read_and_convert([datasets.fetch("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522H.xtf")], fmt="xtf")
a = jsf.get_frequency("hz_521000").dataset["backscatter_intensity"]
b = xtf.get_frequency(sorted(xtf.frequencies)[0]).dataset["backscatter_intensity"]
n_ping = min(a.sizes["ping"], b.sizes["ping"])
n_sample = min(a.sizes["sample"], b.sizes["sample"])
a = a.isel(ping=slice(0, n_ping), sample=slice(0, n_sample)).values
b = b.isel(ping=slice(0, n_ping), sample=slice(0, n_sample)).values
print(f"JSF vs XTF, {n_ping} pings: max |difference| = {np.nanmax(np.abs(a - b)):.3g}")

The last part reads the same EdgeTech pings twice: Discover wrote the line both as JSF and as XTF. The two readers return identical samples:

JSF vs XTF, 288 pings: max |difference| = 0

Data: JNCC Wight-Barfleur Reef and mid-Irish Sea (Open Government Licence v3.0) and USGS Grand Bay (U.S. public domain); see the example data.

docs.title: sidescanpy.datasets
docs.text:
Openly licensed sidescan recordings for examples and tests.

Each registered file is one raw recording inside a public agency archive (a multi-gigabyte zip). :func:fetch pulls just that member out with HTTP range requests, checks its SHA-256 and caches it, so an example needs a few tens of megabytes instead of the whole archive.

from sidescanpy import datasets path = datasets.fetch("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf") print(datasets.citation("jncc_wight_barfleur_20130321174522.jsf"))

The cache is SIDESCANPY_DATA_DIR when set, otherwise ~/.cache/sidescanpy ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/sidescanpy if that is set). A file already in the cache with the right checksum is used as is, so a directory of pre-downloaded files works offline.

Only standard-library modules are used. Downloads log at DEBUG; call :func:sidescanpy.log.configure_logging with "DEBUG" to see them.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: sidescanpy.log
docs.text:
Logging helpers for sidescanpy.

Policy: library modules only create logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) and log at DEBUG (parameters used, defaults applied, fallbacks) or WARNING (real data problems). They never configure handlers and never print. Entry points (the sidescan-* CLIs, consumer scripts) call :func:configure_logging once to decide what is shown and where.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

    level: int | str = "INFO",
    *,
    log_file: str | Path | None = None,
    library_level: int | str | None = None,
    fmt: str | None = None,
) -> None

Configure the root logger for a command-line or script entry point.

Installs a stderr stream handler (and a file handler if log_file is given) on the root logger at level. library_level sets the sidescanpy logger's own level (e.g. "DEBUG" for -v) while leaving third-party loggers at level; None lets it inherit. Noisy third-party loggers are always held at WARNING. Safe to call repeatedly: handlers from a previous call are replaced.
