docs.title: sidescanpy.io
docs.text:
IO for SideScan sonar surveys.

Format-specific readers/converters live in submodules (sidescanpy.io.jsf, sidescanpy.io.sdf, sidescanpy.io.xtf, sidescanpy.io.hdf5, sidescanpy.io.netcdf). This top-level package additionally exposes format-dispatching helpers for callers that have file paths and don't want to branch on extension themselves.

Public entry points
  • :func:detect_format — extension-based format dispatch (.jsf / .sdf / .xtf).
  • :func:read_and_convert — read + convert a list of same-format sonar files into a validated :class:~sidescanpy.core.survey.SideScanSurvey.
  • :func:read_and_convert_segments — one raw file into (output_stem, survey) pairs; XTF files are split at range-setting changes.
  • :func:segment_stem — the output stem of one segment.
  • :func:find_sonar_files — raw sonar files in a directory.
  • :func:load_survey — a .ss.h5 or raw file, whichever it is.
  • :func:detect_catalog_format / :func:read_target_catalog — target catalogs (EdgeTech Discover or Klein SonarWiz), by directory contents.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.dispatch
docs.text:
Format-dispatching helpers for sonar file ingestion.

Given a list of file paths, pick the right per-format reader/converter by extension and produce a validated SideScanSurvey. Used by any script or caller that wants "just give me a survey from these files" without hand-rolling the .jsf/.sdf/.xtf branch itself.

  • :func:detect_format, :func:read_and_convert -- raw .jsf/.sdf/ .xtf.
  • :func:read_and_convert_segments -- one raw file into one or more surveys, each with its output stem (XTF files are split at range-setting changes).
  • :func:find_sonar_files -- the raw files in a directory.
  • :func:load_survey -- a .ss.h5 or a raw file, whichever it is.
  • :func:detect_catalog_format, :func:read_target_catalog -- target catalogs, dispatched on the catalog directory's own contents.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

Read one raw sonar file into one survey per constant-range segment.

A .jsf file gives one survey, exactly as :func:read_and_convert. .xtf and .sdf files are split at sample-rate (range-setting) changes (:func:~sidescanpy.io.xtf.split_by_sample_rate, :func:~sidescanpy.io.sdf.split.split_by_sample_rate) and each kept run is converted on its own, so every survey has the right sample_rate_hz; runs shorter than min_pings are dropped (for XTF, counted in each survey's xtf_pings_dropped_short_runs attribute).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default path Path

required survey_name str

None min_pings int

XTF and SDF: shortest run kept when a file is split.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.hdf5
docs.text:
HDF5 IO for full SideScanSurvey objects.

This module reads and writes complete :class:SideScanSurvey objects — multiple frequency channels plus optional navigation, attitude, DVL, and sensor auxiliary records — as a single .ss.h5 file with a grouped layout.

For single-frequency channels in standalone NetCDF, see :mod:sidescanpy.io.netcdf.

Public entry points
  • :func:read_survey — read a .ss.h5 file back into a validated survey. Accepts chunks= for lazy/dask-backed loading of frequency channel data.

  • :func:write_survey — write a survey to disk with grouped layout and per-variable encoding.

  • :func:read_survey_dir, :func:load_channel_dataset, :func:available_frequencies, :func:concat_survey_frequency — multi-file directory reading (see survey_dir).

  • :func:check_disk_space, :func:atomic_write_survey — in-place rewrite support.
File layout

::

/                           (root: survey_name, source_format,
│                            source_files_json)
/frequencies/
    hz_<freq>/              (per SideScanFrequencyChannel)
    ...
/aux_streams/
    navigation/             (always written, may be empty)
    attitude/
    dvl/
    sensors/
        <sensor_type>/      (only if any sensors present)
Conventions
  • Engine: h5netcdf.
  • Aux records always written, even when empty (zero obs). The reader returns them as empty-but-valid datasets; has_navigation/has_attitude/has_dvl correctly report False in that case.
  • Compression: gzip level 4 on backscatter only. Aux records are tiny and stored uncompressed.
  • chunks= applies only to frequency channels. Aux records always load eagerly regardless.

See docs/io_hdf5.md for full reference.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.jsf
docs.text:
JSF (Edgetech Survey Format) IO.

This module parses Edgetech .jsf binary files into typed message instances and converts those messages into a validated :class:SideScanSurvey.

Public entry points
  • :func:read_jsf — eager read, returns list[JSFMessage].
  • :func:read_jsf_iter — generator over messages (use for large files).
  • :func:convert — dispatches a message list into a :class:SideScanSurvey.
  • :func:write_subset — copy a run of pings to a new file, byte for byte.
Conventions
  • Sonar messages expose timestamp_ns: int. Auxiliary messages expose timestamp: float (epoch seconds).
  • Per-ping fields with invalid validity flags currently appear as None; the converter coerces them to np.nan.
  • All output time coordinates are datetime64[ns].

See docs/io_jsf.md for full reference and known issues.

docs.title: PitchRollDataMessage dataclass
docs.text:
Bases: JSFMessage

Attitude sensor reading (JSF message type 2020).

Body layout per the EdgeTech JSF spec (44 bytes, little endian): int32 seconds since 1970, int32 milliseconds in the current second, 4 reserved bytes, int16 acceleration x/y/z (x 201.5/32768 G), int16 rate gyro x/y/z (x 5001.5/32768 deg/s), int16 pitch and roll (x 180/32768 deg; bow up and port up positive), int16 temperature (0.1 degC), uint16 device-specific info, int16 heave (mm, positive down), uint16 heading (0.01 deg), int32 validity flags, int16 yaw (0.01 deg), int16 reserved.

A derived field is set only when its validity bit is set (bit 0-2 acceleration x/y/z, 3-5 rate x/y/z, 6 pitch, 7 roll, 8 heave, 9 heading, 10 temperature, 11 device info, 12 yaw); otherwise it stays None. Devices are known to clear bits for sensors they lack (for example heave and yaw) while setting pitch, roll and heading.

docs.title: calculate_dvl_altitude_plane_fit
docs.text:
calculate_dvl_altitude_plane_fit(
    beam_distances, beam_angle=20.0
)

Calculate altitude, pitch, and roll from DVL 4-beam distances using plane fitting.

This method fits a plane to the 4 beam endpoints and extracts: - Altitude (vertical distance to the fitted plane) - Pitch (rotation about cross-track axis) - Roll (rotation about along-track axis)

DVL beams are typically arranged in a Janus configuration: - Beam 1: Forward-starboard (+x, +y) - Beam 2: Aft-starboard (-x, +y) - Beam 3: Aft-port (-x, -y) - Beam 4: Forward-port (+x, -y)

Parameters:

beam_distances : array-like Bottom distances for 4 beams, shape (n_samples, 4) or (4,) beam_angle : float Beam angle from vertical in degrees (default: 20.0)

Returns:

results : dict Dictionary containing: - 'altitude': Vertical distance to bottom plane (m) - 'pitch': Pitch angle from plane fit (degrees, positive = bow down) - 'roll': Roll angle from plane fit (degrees, positive = starboard down) - 'altitude_std': RMS residual of plane fit (m) - 'altitude_per_beam': Vertical distance for each beam (m) - 'bottom_points': 3D coordinates of beam endpoints (m) - 'plane_normal': Unit normal vector of fitted plane - 'quality_flag': 0=good, 1=suspect, 2=bad (insufficient beams)

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.jsf.targets
docs.text:
EdgeTech Discover SQLite .target catalog reader.

Discover writes one SQLite database per target pick (Target-NNNN.target), holding a raw JSF ping-sample window plus position metadata. Schema (Target, PingChannel, MutableTarget, MutableTag tables) was reverse-engineered by hand and verified against real Discover target files.

Known gotchas this reader accounts for:

  • Target.TargetId is a per-file primary key that always resets to 1 — never a cross-file identifier. The real identity is the filename's own number (Target-NNNN.target), used as Target.target_id here.
  • PingChannel's ~200-row window is usually a clean contiguous run of PingSequenceNumber values, but not always. One real file seen so far (Target-0002.target) has two things wrong at once: (1) a uint32 rollover artifact — 104 of its rows, and the target's own MutableTarget.PingSequenceNumber, are stored as true_value + 2**32 (e.g. raw 4294971779 for a true 4483, confirmed by the corrected value's neighbors forming a clean contiguous run); (2) an unrelated, disjoint cluster of 94 rows (4846-4939) mixed into the same file's PingChannel table, nowhere near the target's real window. Correcting the rollover and then walking outward from the target's own (corrected) ping to find its contiguous run handles both at once — no fixed distance threshold from the target's raw ping is reliable here, since the target's own raw value is exactly what's corrupted. position_confidence downgrades to "approximate" (recording the exclusion in extra_attributes) whenever this filtering actually removes rows.
  • MutableTarget.Description/MutableTag.Tag are commonly empty — this is normal (no classification was ever recorded), not a read failure; label stays None rather than a placeholder string.

Position formula (validated visually against 6+ real targets): within the ping window sorted by sequence number, the target's row is the index of its own PingSequenceNumber; its column is round(SlantRangeDistanceMeters / PingMetersPerSample) using the target's own ping's PingMetersPerSample (not a window-wide constant, though it typically doesn't vary within one window).

Decode (:func:decode_target_window; raw values, native orientation -- TVG and display orientation live in export.target_window): SampleBytes -> np.frombuffer(dtype="<i2").astype(float) * 2 ** (-JsfWeightingFactor) — real JSF sample amplitudes, not a rendered image. Expect a leading run of exact-zero samples (blanking/ring-down); not a bug.

NetCDF IO for single-frequency channels.

Public entry points

Conventions

  • Compression: gzip level 4 on per-sample variables (e.g. backscatter_intensity). Per-ping scalars uncompressed.
  • Chunking: HDF5_CHUNK_PING along the ping axis on disk. Override on read via chunks={"ping": N}.
  • Round-trip is bit-exact for variable values, attributes, and processing_history.

See docs/io_netcdf.md for full reference.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf
docs.text:
Klein Marine Systems SDF (Sonar Data File) reader.

Parses Edgetech-style SDF files: a sequence of fixed-format pages, each with a 4-byte sync marker followed by a 512-byte header and variable- length sonar data.

This module provides:

  • :class:SDFSonarPage — typed dataclass for sonar data pages (versions 3501 and 3502; low- and high-frequency channels).
  • :func:parse_page_header — parse 516 bytes of header into a typed page, dispatching by page version.
  • :func:read_sdf / :func:read_sdf_iter — read pages from a file.
  • :func:convert — convert pages into a SideScanSurvey.

Klein conventions captured here:

  • Position fields (latitude/longitude) are stored as float64 in radians; this module converts to degrees on parse.
  • Attitude fields (heading/pitch/roll) are stored as float32 in degrees; no unit conversion needed.
  • Page sizes in the header exclude the 4-byte marker; total page on disk is page_size_field + 4.
  • Year is normally 4-digit (e.g. 2026); some firmware stores offset-from-1900. Auto-detected via < 200 check.

See docs/io_sdf.md for full reference.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf.converter
docs.text:
Convert Klein SDF pages into a SideScanSurvey.

The converter takes pages (typically from read_sdf or read_sdf_iter) and builds a validated SideScanSurvey with:

  • One SideScanFrequencyChannel per distinct center_freq_hz
  • Per-ping fields (latitude, longitude, heading, pitch, roll, depth, altitude, fathometer_reading) extracted from each page's header
  • Navigation aux record from per-page (timestamp, lat, lon)
  • Attitude aux record from per-page (timestamp, heading, pitch, roll)
  • Empty DVL record (Klein doesn't have DVL)
  • No sensor records (Klein doesn't have ancillary sensor streams)

The reader yields both SDFSonarPage (sonar versions 3501/3502) and SDFUnknownPage (everything else). The converter filters to sonar pages only with an info log; non-sonar pages are dropped silently.

Klein-specific design decisions:

  • depth_m is set to NaN. The spec stores depth in Volts (field 31), and conversion to meters requires calibration data from the INI file that we don't currently parse. Users with calibration can override.
  • sound_vel_ms per ping is NaN (Klein doesn't provide sound velocity).
  • heave_m per ping is NaN (Klein doesn't provide heave).
  • altitude_m is currently a copy of fathometer_reading_m (no attitude correction yet).
  • sample_rate_hz is computed from the first page's (num_samples, range_m) assuming 1500 m/s sound velocity.
  • pulse_length_us is 0.0 (not provided by Klein).
  • freq_hz_start == freq_hz_end == center_freq_hz.
  • Pages with different num_samples are padded to max with NaN, logged as a warning when it happens. Each ping's true recorded sample count survives padding via the valid_samples (ping, channel) variable, so downstream code (e.g. processing/farrange.py) can distinguish real short pings from padded filler rather than treating the padded array shape as if every ping genuinely recorded that many samples.
  • convert() builds one array per call across every page it's handed. Current callers (io/dispatch.py: read_and_convert()) invoke it once per source file (01_convert.py calls read_and_convert([single_path], ...) in a loop), so in practice padding is currently scoped to pages within one physical .sdf file. read_and_convert()'s own multi-file-merge capability would pad across files too if a caller ever used it that way — worth knowing before doing so, not a hidden trap given the warning above, but a single outlier-length page anywhere in whatever set of pages reaches this function does inflate every other page's stored array.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf.pages
docs.text:
Klein SDF page types and parser.

A Klein SDF file is a sequence of pages. Each page has: - A 4-byte sync marker (always 0xFFFFFFFF) - A 512-byte typed header (described by SDFPageHeader) - Variable-length data section (sonar samples for sonar page versions)

The header is a binary structure of 128 uint32-equivalent slots. Most fields are uint32 or float32 (4 bytes); seven fields are float64 (8 bytes, taking 2 slots). All values are little-endian.

Spec source: Klein SDF/SDFX Data Page Definitions Specification.

Conventions encoded here: - Latitude/longitude stored as float64 in radians; converted to degrees via @property - Heading/pitch/roll stored as float32 in degrees; no conversion - speedFish stored as cm/s; converted to m/s via @property - speedSound stored as cm/s; converted to m/s via @property - sonarFreq stored in kHz; converted to Hz via @property - Year normally 4-digit; older firmware uses offset-from-1900, auto-detected via < 200 check - Time fractional component (fseconds field 51) preferred over hSecond field 24 when both are valid

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: SDFPageHeader dataclass
docs.text:
Klein SDF page header (512 bytes after the 4-byte marker).

All fields are little-endian. The dataclass holds the raw spec values; transformed (unit-converted) versions are exposed via @property.

Field numbers in comments correspond to the Klein spec table (1-100 named, 101-126 reserved). Fields prefixed with underscore are internal raw forms with corresponding public properties.

Note on uint16 fields (80-83): the spec says U16 but Klein stores them in 32-bit slots with values fitting in the lower 16 bits. They're parsed as uint32 here for layout purity.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf.reader
docs.text:
Klein SDF file reader.

Iterates pages in a Klein SDF file. Each page has: - A 4-byte sync marker (always 0xFFFFFFFF) - A 512-byte typed header (described by SDFPageHeader) - Variable-length body (sonar samples for sonar pages, raw bytes otherwise)

The reader handles file-level concerns: marker validation, header parsing, page-version dispatch, and sample data extraction. The pages module defines what a page IS (typed structures); the reader handles WHERE pages are.

Three entry points: - read_sdf_header(f): low-level, reads marker + header at current position - read_sdf(path): eager, returns list of all pages (sonar + unknown) - read_sdf_iter(path): lazy, yields pages one at a time

On a bad marker, logs a warning and scans forward (up to 1 MB) looking for the next valid marker. This is robust to small corruption, mid-page truncation, or our own header parsing errors.

For sonar pages, the body is parsed into port and starboard sample arrays, with any remaining bytes preserved in extension_bytes for future decoding. For non-sonar pages, the entire body is preserved in body_bytes.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf.split
docs.text:
Split one Klein SDF file's pages into runs of constant sample interval.

The range setting can change mid-file. Klein keeps the metres per sample of a frequency only when the sample count scales with the range; on some recorders it does not (for example 2500 samples at 60 m, then 3334 at 40 m), so the sample interval changes. The survey model has one sample_rate_hz per frequency (computed by the converter from the first page), so such a file cannot become one survey without mapping some pings to the wrong range. :func:split_by_sample_rate cuts the pages into consecutive runs (in file order) within which every frequency keeps its sample rate, each run converted on its own by :func:sidescanpy.io.sdf.convert.

Cut rule (same as the XTF split): a frequency's rate is num_samples / range_m (proportional to the sample rate at constant sound speed). A run's reference rate for a frequency is the first one it records; a page whose rate differs from that reference by more than rtol (relative) starts a new run, for every frequency. Pages without a positive range do not take part. Runs with fewer than min_pings pages of their most-recorded frequency are dropped (a range change often leaves a few pings at an intermediate setting); a file without a cut is kept whole.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.sdf.targets
docs.text:
Klein/SonarWiz native target catalog reader (Target_<unix_ts>.tgt / .tgd pairs).

Reverse-engineered from real files; not vendor-documented. No independent reference exists to check field meanings against — validation consisted of rendering the raw window and checking that a candidate field lands on a visible sonar contact, not a byte-for-byte spec match. Every Target produced here gets position_confidence="unknown" unconditionally, regardless of which fields below are confirmed — that flag is about absolute geographic position (never found in this format at all, see below), not about whether the on-image box placement is trustworthy.

What's confirmed (byte-exact, cross-checked across multiple real files):

  • .tgt is not a documented catalog format itself, but file(1) identifies it as a dBase-IV memo (.DBT) block file, and its content is consistent with that: a small fixed header, then a run of length-prefixed UTF-16LE string fields (each starting with the 3-byte marker FF FE FF then a 1-byte character count), then a fixed-layout binary trailer once the strings end.
  • The file's own Unix timestamp (from its filename, Target_<ts>.tgt) appears verbatim as a little-endian int32 at byte offset 8 — confirms the header is being read correctly and the timestamp is the pick time, not an arbitrary filename.
  • .tgd is a fixed-size raw sonar window: an 8-byte header (int32 n_channels, int32 n_samples — read as (2, 2500) on the one real survey checked, matching that survey's own converted .ss.h5 sample count exactly), followed by (n_pings, n_channels, n_samples) int16 amplitude — real backscatter data, confirmed by a plausible leading-saturation run (same shape as the leading-blanking-run artifact sidescanpy already knows about from JSF data) and by-eye inspection of the decoded window showing genuine seafloor texture.

What's confirmed by visual cross-check:

  • window_row: the raw trailer int32 (ints[5]) is 2x the true row — this module halves it before returning. Confirmed against six real targets by rendering each one's full decoded window with no box, locating the visible sonar contact by eye, and checking which candidate row landed on it. Five of six checks landed cleanly on a visible feature; one landed in a relatively low-contrast area (the column could be off for that target, or it is a weak contact). Why the field is 2x is unknown.
  • slant_range_m and a constant max_window_range_m (varies by survey file, e.g. 40.0 or 60.0 seen so far): a float32 slot that varies per target in a plausible tens-of-meters range, paired with a float32 slot that's identical across every target in one file. max_window_range_m / n_samples gives a plausible meters-per-sample constant, used to convert slant_range_m into a window column index. Not contradicted by any of the six row-validation checks above (the column landed in the right vicinity in every case), but never independently verified the way window_row has been.

What's inferred, not confirmed (best-effort field mapping in the binary trailer that follows the string fields, found by comparing several real files and noting which int32/float32 slots vary plausibly vs. stay constant):

  • channel (0/1): an int32 slot that's always exactly 0 or 1; 0 = port, 1 = starboard. Confirmed on real catalogs: the .tgd window matches the survey's own pings on that side.
  • The string fields ahead of the trailer are kept verbatim in extra_attributes["string_fields"]: ping time, ping number (both interpreted below), a decimal number (not interpreted), the target name, and a notes field. The notes field is the unedited placeholder text ("The operator places target notes here. Multiple lines OK.") on every real target checked so far, not a real label.

Catalog ping time and number (confirmed on real catalogs by matching every .tgd window back to the survey's own pings):

  • String field 0 is the date-time (M/D/YYYY h:mm:ss) and field 1 the ping number of the target's own ping, both on the sonar's own clock, the same clock as the pings in the .sdf files (which can be years off real time). Parsed into extra_attributes["catalog_ping_time"] (Unix seconds on that clock, 1 s resolution) and extra_attributes["catalog_ping_number"]. Ping counters can restart after a recording gap, so the number alone is not unique; the time disambiguates. Use :func:sidescanpy.targets.correlate.resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping to place targets: it needs no clock offset.
  • pick_timestamp (the Target_<unix> file name) is when the pick was saved, on the acquisition PC's clock: typically 30-90 s after the target ping, and hours later for picks made during playback. Matching pings by it places targets tens to hundreds of metres along track from where they are.
  • The .tgd window holds the catalog channel of the high-frequency data, one row per second ping, newest ping first. window_row counts rows from the top, so its ping is newest - 2 * window_row. On real catalogs this lands on the catalog ping for about three quarters of the targets; for the rest it is several to ~100 pings older, so window_row is not a reliable target ping. sample (from the range field) has been consistent.
  • Some picks are made from the live display while logging is off; their catalog time falls in a recording gap and the .tgd is the only copy of that data.

No absolute latitude/longitude was found anywhere in .tgt (searched exhaustively for plausible float32/float64 pairs in the survey area's lat/lon range — none found). Position must be resolved externally, e.g. by matching pick_timestamp against a converted survey's own per-ping timestamps (see sidescanpy.targets.correlate.resolve_target_position) — this is a nearest-ping approximation, not a stored pick position, and does not upgrade position_confidence above "unknown".

Parsing only: position resolution and clock-offset calibration against converted .ss.h5 files live in :mod:sidescanpy.targets.correlate.

Row target.extra_attributes["window_row"] is the catalog's box row, which is not always the target's own ping (see module docstring); column target.sample is the target's sample within each ping.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.xtf.converter
docs.text:
Convert XTF sonar pings into a SideScanSurvey.

Takes the per-file output of :func:sidescanpy.io.xtf.read_xtf (one :class:~sidescanpy.io.xtf.reader.XtfPingData per file) and builds a validated survey shaped like the JSF and SDF ones:

  • One frequency channel per port/starboard pair sharing a ChanInfo frequency, keyed hz_<Hz>. ChanInfo.Frequency is in kHz (the per-channel header's Frequency is a 16-bit kHz value too); a value of 10 000 or more cannot be a sidescan frequency in kHz and is taken as Hz (logged at DEBUG).
  • backscatter_intensity is (ping, channel, sample) float32 with channel 0 = port, 1 = starboard. Samples beyond a ping's NumSamples and a side absent from a ping are NaN; valid_samples (ping, channel) holds the recorded count (0 where absent), as in the SDF converter. Sample 0 is nearest the sonar on both sides: XTF stores port samples far -> near (so [port | stbd] reads as one across-track line), and the converter reverses each port ping's valid samples. Verified on real EdgeTech 4200 files: the first bottom return of the reversed port data tracks SensorPrimaryAltitude the way the starboard data does as stored.
  • Samples are multiplied by 2**-Weight from each channel header. EdgeTech Discover writes the raw block-floating-point samples and puts the JSF weighting factor N in Weight, which can change from ping to ping; scaling makes the samples equal to the JSF ones for the same ping (checked on a public Discover 7.22 recording with both files). Writers that leave Weight at 0 are unaffected. The range seen is recorded in xtf_weight_min / xtf_weight_max.
  • Each frequency has its own ping axis. A ping holding neither channel of a frequency (some files' early packets carry only the low-frequency pair, see :mod:sidescanpy.io.xtf.reader) is left out of that frequency, logged at DEBUG and counted in the xtf_pings_absent attribute.
  • Per-ping fields come from the ping header: SensorYcoordinate / SensorXcoordinate → latitude / longitude (degrees, NavUnits 3 only), SensorHeading, SensorPitch (positive nose up), SensorRoll (positive roll to starboard, i.e. port up, the JSF convention), Heave, SensorDepth → heading_deg, pitch_deg, roll_deg, heave_m, depth_m. SensorPrimaryAltitude → altitude_m and fathometer_reading_m, with 0 (no bottom lock) as NaN, the way the JSF converter turns an invalid altitude into NaN.
  • Times from Year … Second + HSeconds (10 ms resolution, the recorder's time base, normally UTC).
Sound velocity and sample rate

Some recorders write half the sound velocity in SoundVelocity (the one-way factor c / 2). A value below 1000 m/s is not a plausible sound speed in water, so it is doubled (logged at DEBUG); a plausible value is kept. Where the channel header gives both SlantRange and TimeDuration the choice is cross-checked against SlantRange / TimeDuration (which is c / 2) and a disagreement over 5 % logged at WARNING. Zero or negative values become NaN, so downstream code falls back to 1500 m/s as for SDF.

sample_rate_hz is NumSamples / TimeDuration (falling back to NumSamples * c / (2 * SlantRange) when TimeDuration is 0), so the slant range of the last sample, n * c / (2 * fs), equals TimeDuration * c / 2. The survey model has one sample rate per frequency. Files whose range setting changes mid-file (the sample count staying fixed) are meant to be split first with :func:sidescanpy.io.xtf.split_by_sample_rate and each run converted on its own. When unsplit pings still mix rates, the most common rate is used and the pings at other rates are reported at WARNING and counted in xtf_pings_other_sample_rate; their ranges are then wrong by the ratio of the rates. For split runs the tolerance is twice the split's rtol, so the WARNING does not fire for them.

Not converted: pulse_length_us is not in the XTF ping or channel headers and is 0.0 (as for SDF); gain codes are not interpreted. NavUnits 0 (projected coordinates) raises NotImplementedError: neither the JSF nor the SDF converter has a projected-coordinate path.

Provenance attributes on every frequency dataset (xtf_ prefix): recording program and version, sonar name and type, channel numbers and names, whether sound velocity was doubled, the Weight range, and counts of reader anomalies summed over the converted files (packets with fewer channel blocks than declared, clipped channel blocks, channel blocks without ChanInfo, unknown and non-sonar packets, resyncs, truncated files). A single split run (XtfPingData.segment set) adds xtf_segment_index and xtf_segment_count (1-based, kept runs of the file), xtf_segment_ping_start / xtf_segment_ping_stop (its half-open range in the file's sonar pings), xtf_file_pings, and xtf_runs_dropped_short / xtf_pings_dropped_short_runs (runs of the file shorter than the split's min_pings, and their pings).

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.xtf.reader
docs.text:
Low-level XTF (eXtended Triton Format) reader.

Reads the file header, frames packets, and parses sonar packets into per-ping header records and per-channel sample arrays. The converter to the standard survey model is sidescanpy.io.xtf.converter; read_xtf is the per-file entry point that feeds it.

File layout

A file starts with a 1024-byte header holding up to six ChanInfo channel descriptions; with more than six channels the remaining ChanInfo entries follow contiguously in further 1024-byte blocks. Packets follow. Each starts with the magic 0xFACE, a header type and NumBytesThisRecord, the packet's total size including any padding. That byte count is authoritative: the reader steps from packet to packet with it, never with sizes derived from the packet contents. A packet with a bad magic triggers a forward scan for the next 0xFACE (counted, and logged at WARNING); a truncated final packet is logged at WARNING and ends the read.

A sonar packet (header type 0) is a 256-byte ping header followed, for each channel, by a 64-byte channel header and NumSamples samples. The sample type comes from the file header's ChanInfo entry for that channel (SampleFormat, else BytesPerSample).

Channel blocks are walked using the packet byte count

NumChansToFollow in the ping header is treated as an upper bound. Channel blocks are parsed while at least a full 64-byte channel header remains inside the packet; a channel whose samples would run past the packet end is clipped to the samples that fit. Each mismatch kind is logged at WARNING once per file with a count.

Evidence for this rule (EdgeTech 4200 files recorded by Isis, four channels declared in the file header: port/starboard at 120 kHz as channels 0/1 and at 410 kHz as channels 2/3, BytesPerSample 2):

  • In two such files the first sonar packets (2976 of 25539 in one file, 1680 of 20475 in the other, a single contiguous run at the start) are 4480 bytes long while their ping headers say NumChansToFollow = 4 and the first two channel headers say NumSamples = 1024. Normal packets are 8704 = 256 + 4 * (64 + 1024 * 2) bytes.
  • 4480 = 256 + 2 * (64 + 1024 * 2) exactly: the packet holds two complete channel blocks (channel numbers 0 and 1, the low-frequency pair) and nothing else. The "third channel header" a reader trusting NumChansToFollow would parse starts with 0xFACE: it is the next packet.
  • The samples are 16-bit, 1024 per channel as declared. Read as uint16, adjacent samples correlate (lag-1 r = 0.96 and 0.79 over the two runs, 0.86 and 0.80 in the same files' normal pings), values stay within the normal pings' 0..32767 range, and medians are comparable (1148 vs 1505, 285 vs 731). Read as 8-bit, adjacent samples do not correlate (r = -0.01 and -0.46). The first pings of each run are faint (high byte zero in 88-99.99 % of the first 200 pings), rising to the normal level. Ping numbers are continuous across the switch to four-channel packets, navigation is continuous, and the low-only pings repeat faster (0.08 s vs 0.14 s at 100 m range, 0.21 s vs 0.42 s at 300 m).

So those pings carry only the low-frequency pair; the high-frequency channels are absent, not empty. pyxtf 1.5.0 trusts NumChansToFollow and fails on such packets.

Sample arrays

Samples keep their recorded dtype (uint8/uint16/uint32/float32), so values are bit-identical to the file. A channel's array is (n_ping, max_samples) over all sonar pings of the file; pings where the channel is absent or shorter are zero-padded on the right, and the true length is in num_samples (0 where absent, with present False). The converter decides whether padding becomes NaN.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.xtf.split
docs.text:
Split XTF pings into runs of constant sample interval.

Some recorders keep a fixed number of samples per ping and change the range setting mid-file, so the sample interval (TimeDuration / NumSamples) changes from one ping to the next. The survey model has one sample_rate_hz per frequency, so a file like that cannot become one survey without giving some pings the wrong range. :func:split_by_sample_rate cuts the pings of one file into consecutive runs (in file order) within which every channel keeps its sample rate, each run an :class:~sidescanpy.io.xtf.reader.XtfPingData that :func:sidescanpy.io.xtf.convert turns into its own survey.

Cut rule

For each port/starboard channel the per-ping sample rate is NumSamples / TimeDuration (NumSamples / SlantRange, proportional at constant sound speed, when a channel never records TimeDuration). A run's reference rate for a channel is the first rate it records in the run; a ping whose rate differs from that reference by more than rtol (relative) starts a new run. Comparing with the run's reference rather than the previous ping stops a slow drift from accumulating inside a run. Pings where a channel is absent (present False) or carries no usable rate do not take part for that channel, so they never cause a cut. A cut in any channel cuts every channel.

Runs shorter than min_pings are dropped (a range change usually leaves a few pings at an intermediate setting). A file without a cut is returned whole whatever its length.

Each run is a view of the file's arrays (no copy, no re-read). A channel absent from every ping of a run is left out of that run, so a run may hold fewer frequencies than the file. stats and block_stats are the whole file's. segment (:class:XtfSegmentInfo) records where the run sits in the file; the converter turns it into xtf_ provenance attributes.

docs.title: sidescanpy.io.xtf.structs
docs.text:
XTF binary structures as numpy structured dtypes.

Field names, order and sizes follow the eXtended Triton Format specification, revision 42 (Exail), and agree field for field with the ctypes structures in pyxtf 1.5.0 (checked by the unit tests). All structures are little-endian and packed (no alignment padding); each dtype's itemsize is asserted at import.

Structures
  • CHAN_INFO_DTYPE (128 bytes): one channel description in the file header (CHANINFO).
  • FILE_HEADER_DTYPE (1024 bytes): the file header (XTFFILEHEADER) including its first six ChanInfo blocks.
  • PACKET_START_DTYPE (14 bytes): the fields every packet starts with (magic 0xFACE, header type, sub-channel, channels to follow, reserved, total packet byte count).
  • PING_HEADER_DTYPE (256 bytes): the sonar ping header (XTFPINGHEADER); its first 14 bytes are the packet start fields.
  • PING_CHAN_HEADER_DTYPE (64 bytes): the per-channel header (XTFPINGCHANHEADER) that precedes each channel's samples.

Units as given by the specification (the reader does not convert): times in seconds, ranges in metres, SensorDepth / SensorPrimaryAltitude in metres, angles in degrees, ShipAltitude / ShipDepth in decimetres, coordinates in the units named by the file header's NavUnits (0 = projected metres, 3 = degrees with X = longitude, Y = latitude). Sound-velocity fields may hold half the true value (some recorders store the one-way factor c / 2).

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing
docs.text:
Processing functions for SideScan sonar surveys.

Each function takes a validated input dataset, applies a transform, and returns a new dataset with updated values, processing_level, and processing_history. Functions are pure (no in-place mutation by default) unless explicitly marked otherwise.

Public entry points
  • :func:interpolate_aux_onto_pings — replace per-ping nav, attitude, and heave fields with values interpolated from the survey's auxiliary records onto each ping's timestamp.
  • :func:held_value_fixes — reduce a sample-and-hold aux record (the latest fix repeated at every ping or packet) to its real fixes; the interpolate_aux step does this by default.
  • :func:aux_update_events — change and update-event statistics of a sample-and-hold record, for choosing groups and merge_window_s.
  • :func:interpolate_onto_channel — lower-level: interpolate any xr.Dataset (e.g. an external GPS log) onto one channel's ping times.
  • :func:along_track_distance_m, :func:fill_nav_stalls — cumulative along-track distance from ping lat/lon, and nav-stall repair.
  • :func:apply_tvg — apply time-varying gain (spreading + absorption) to backscatter. Converts raw linear amplitude to dB.
  • :func:apply_tvg_to_amplitude — same TVG correction as :func:apply_tvg, but on a plain (..., n_samples) array rather than a full xr.Dataset — for data that isn't a survey channel (e.g. a target catalog's own decoded crop window).
  • :func:francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m / :func:absorption_for_frequency — seawater absorption (Francois-Garrison) defaults for typical coastal seawater.
  • :func:correct, :func:correct_survey, :func:correct_file — the one correction API: an ordered list of built-in or caller-supplied steps, each skippable, idempotent and recorded in processing_history (see :mod:sidescanpy.processing.correct).
  • :func:invert, :func:uncorrected_backscatter — undo recorded steps from their history records.
  • :func:processing_level — derived from processing_history.
  • Bottom / nadir handling (:mod:~sidescanpy.processing.bottom): :func:detect_first_bottom_return, :func:altitude_from_bottom_track (the "bottom_track" step), :func:detect_nadir_noise_extent, :func:blank_nadir_noise, :func:mask_nadir_gap, :func:uniform_exclusion_boundary and helpers.
  • :func:reject_range_outliers — per-range-bin MAD outlier rejection.
  • :func:mask_bright_ping_rows — mask whole outlier-bright ping rows.
  • Segments (:mod:~sidescanpy.processing.segments): :func:find_segments, :func:split_by_segments, :class:Segment and the individual detectors.
  • :func:backscatter_vs_range / :func:backscatter_vs_sample — binned backscatter profiles.
  • :func:build_survey_track / :class:SurveyTrack — nadir track plus strided swath-edge positions across a multi-file survey.
Conventions
  • Corrections are applied in place to backscatter_intensity; no raw copy is kept (a legacy backscatter_raw is dropped on rewrite).
  • Every correction step appends one processing_history record with the parameters it used; a step already recorded is not re-applied.

See docs/processing.md for full reference.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes
docs.text:
Reduce sample-and-hold auxiliary records to the sensor's real fixes.

Many recorders log navigation and attitude as sample-and-hold: every ping or packet carries the latest value the sensor delivered, so the same value repeats until the sensor updates (a ~1 Hz GPS under ~10 Hz pings repeats each position about ten times). Interpolating linearly between those held entries keeps the stair-steps: consecutive pings stack on one position and then jump. :func:held_value_fixes keeps only the entries where a value actually changed, timed where the change most likely happened, so that interpolating the result recovers a smooth track. Some recorders also spread one sensor update over consecutive entries (the bulk change, then a small follow-up one entry later); merge_window_s collapses such changes into one update event, and :func:aux_update_events reports the change and event statistics needed to choose it.

docs.title: held_value_fixes
docs.text:
held_value_fixes(
    record: Dataset,
    *,
    groups: Sequence[Sequence[str]] | None = None,
    max_hold_s: float = 2.0,
    merge_window_s: MergeWindow = None,
) -> xr.Dataset

Keep only the real fixes of a sample-and-hold auxiliary record.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default record Dataset

Auxiliary record with dimension obs and a time coordinate along it (datetime64). Entries need not be sorted.

required groups sequence of sequence of str

Variables that update together. A group's entry is a fix when any of its variables changed. By default every numeric obs variable is its own group, latitude and longitude included: some recorders log the two coordinates of one fix in separate entries a fraction of a second apart, and a joint group would turn each half-update into a fix carrying a stale other coordinate. Pass groups=[POSITION_GROUP] to join them. Variables not named in groups are single-variable groups.

None max_hold_s float

A value unchanged for longer than this (from the first to the last entry that carries it) is treated as a real hold, such as a stop or a sensor dropout: an extra anchor entry keeps the value at the time of the last entry before the change, so interpolation stays flat across the hold instead of ramping through it. np.inf disables anchors. With merge_window_s, the hold is measured from the last change of the update event.

2.0 merge_window_s float or mapping of str to float

Within each group, consecutive changes at most this many seconds apart (chained: each measured from the previous change) collapse into one update event, for recorders that log one sensor update over consecutive entries (the bulk change, then a small follow-up one entry later). The event carries the group's value after its last change and is timed by the fix-time rule applied to its first change (see Notes). Choose a window longer than the follow-up delay and shorter than the real update interval; :func:aux_update_events shows both. A float applies to every group; a mapping {variable: seconds} applies only to the groups holding those variables (a group takes the smallest window of its variables) and leaves the others unmerged, so a window sized for a ~3 Hz GPS does not chain the changes of a ~10 Hz roll sensor into one event. None (default) keeps every change as its own fix. Groups are merged independently.

None

Returns:

Type Description Dataset

A record on a new obs axis: the sorted union of every group's fix and anchor times. A variable is NaN at times that are not one of its own fixes (drop NaN rows per variable before interpolating; the interpolate_aux step does). Variables are float64. The input attrs are kept, plus held_value_fixes_entries_in, held_value_fixes_entries_out, held_value_fixes_dropped (entries in minus out) and held_value_fixes_max_hold_s, plus held_value_fixes_merge_window_s when merge_window_s is set (a float, or a JSON string of the mapping). Non-numeric variables and variables without the obs dimension are left out.

Raises:

Type Description KeyError

If record has no time coordinate, or groups names a variable the record does not have.

ValueError

If max_hold_s is negative or NaN, or a merge_window_s value is negative or not finite.

Notes

Per group, after sorting by time (stable, so logging order is kept within equal times) and dropping entries where any of the group's variables is NaN or the time is NaT:

  • Duplicate timestamps collapse to the last entry logged at that time, the most recent value the logger had. Earlier entries at the same time are superseded, not averaged (averaging a stale and a new value would invent a position, and does not apply to compass angles). When the entries at one time disagree, the update was seen at that time, so a fix there keeps that time.
  • A fix is an entry whose value differs from the previous entry (exact inequality; this is right for compass angles too, which the interpolator unwraps). The first entry is always a fix. NaN entries are never fixes.
  • Fix time. When the previous entry repeated the value before it (the value was being held), the new value arrived somewhere between the two entries, so the fix is placed at their midpoint. When the previous entry was itself a fix, the stream is updating at the logging rate and the entry's own time is kept. A record in which every entry differs from the previous one is therefore returned with its values and times unchanged. The first fix keeps its own time, as does a fix at a duplicated timestamp whose entries disagree.
  • Holds longer than max_hold_s add an anchor (see above), including the hold that ends the record.
  • Merged updates (merge_window_s). The first entry of the record is never merged with what follows: it is the start of the record, not an observed change. An event takes the time its first change would have had as a fix (the midpoint after a hold) and the value after its last change. The first changed entry is when the update started reaching the log; the follow-up entries complete the same update rather than report new motion, so the sensor's fix epoch is best estimated from the first. Timing at the last change instead would add a delay that varies with how many entries an update happened to spread over, which shows up as speed jitter; timing at the first gives a near-constant latency, which leaves speed unbiased. A stream that changes at every entry with entries closer than merge_window_s chains into long events; a WARNING is logged when an event combines more than five changes.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.bottom
docs.text:
Nadir and first-bottom-return detection, and the masks built on them.

Along each ping, a sidescan record runs through three zones: a leading nadir-noise burst (transmit ring-down; some hardware zeros it before writing the file, some doesn't), a quiet span the beam never illuminates, and the real bottom return. The functions here find those boundaries per (ping, channel) and blank or mask the data before them.

  • :func:detect_nadir_noise_extent / :func:blank_nadir_noise — find and zero the leading noise burst (a processing step).
  • :func:detect_first_bottom_return — amplitude-based onset of the real bottom return, optionally floored at the altitude sample.
  • :func:smooth_boundary_across_pings — rolling median of a per-ping boundary.
  • :func:uniform_exclusion_boundary — collapse a per-ping boundary to one conservative value for aggregate binning.
  • :func:mask_nadir_gap — NaN everything before the first bottom return (display/export copy).
  • :func:mask_before_sample, :func:altitude_sample_index — helpers.
  • :func:altitude_from_bottom_track — fill missing altitude_m from the first bottom return (the "bottom_track" correction step).

All detectors are vectorized over (ping, channel, sample) arrays and return (ping, channel) float sample indices (NaN = not found).

docs.title: detect_first_bottom_return
docs.text:
detect_first_bottom_return(
    value_arr: ndarray,
    *,
    smooth_window: int = 10,
    threshold_fraction: float = 0.2,
    min_run: int = 10,
    min_sample: ndarray | float | None = None,
    min_sample_buffer: float = 0.0,
    peak_percentile: float = 100.0,
    min_run_fraction: float = 1.0,
) -> np.ndarray

Per-(ping, channel) sample index where the real bottom return starts.

Smooths each ping with a smooth_window-sample rolling mean, then finds the first point where the smoothed value stays at or above threshold_fraction of that ping's own peak for min_run consecutive samples. The threshold is relative per ping and channel, since amplitude scale varies by channel and survey.

This is not the altitude crossing (slant_range_m > altitude_m): a real beam's near edge is tilted away from vertical, so the first bottom return lands further out than altitude alone predicts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default value_arr ndarray

(ping, channel, sample) linear amplitude (not dB).

required smooth_window int 10 threshold_fraction float

Fraction of the ping's peak smoothed value.

0.2 min_run int

Samples the rise must be sustained for.

10 min_sample array - like or float

Per-(ping, channel) or scalar floor. Samples before it are ignored for both the peak and the onset search. Normally the altitude sample: the bottom can't return before it. NaN entries mean "no floor" for that row.

None min_sample_buffer float

Added to min_sample before use, to step past residual near-nadir noise.

0.0 peak_percentile float

Percentile of the smoothed values used as the peak reference (100 = max). Lower it to stop one bright residual sample from setting the threshold.

100.0 min_run_fraction float

Fraction of the min_run samples that must be at or above the threshold (the onset sample itself always must be). Below 1 a long run tolerates gaps, such as shadows in a rough seabed return.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description ndarray

(ping, channel) float sample index, NaN where no sustained rise was found. Accurate to about smooth_window samples.

docs.title: altitude_from_bottom_track
docs.text:
altitude_from_bottom_track(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    replace: str = "missing",
    max_diff_m: float | None = None,
    min_altitude_m: float = 0.5,
    min_return_m: float = 5.0,
    min_return_fraction: float = 0.7,
    smooth_window: int = 10,
    threshold_fraction: float = 0.2,
    min_run: int = 10,
    smooth_pings: int = 1,
) -> xr.Dataset

Set altitude_m from the first bottom return (the "bottom_track" step).

Many recordings carry no usable altitude: no altimeter, no bottom lock, or a recorder that writes 0. Without it the geometric step cannot compute ground range (NaN altitude) or computes it as if the towfish sat on the seabed (altitude 0). This step measures altitude from the data instead: per ping and channel, the onset of the bottom return (:func:detect_first_bottom_return on the uncorrected amplitude, refined to the first sample reaching half the return level that follows it, since the detector's rolling mean fires up to smooth_window samples early), the nearer of the two channels, converted to metres of slant range.

The first return comes from the beam's near edge, which is tilted away from vertical, so on sloping or rough seabed the tracked value is the slant range to the nearest bottom point, at or slightly above the true altitude. Recorded altitude, when valid, is the better value; the default only fills pings that lack it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

One frequency channel. Radiometric steps already applied are undone for detection only; backscatter_intensity is not changed.

required replace (missing, all)

"missing": replace pings whose altitude_m is NaN or <= 0. "all": replace every ping with a detection.

"missing" max_diff_m float

With "missing", also replace pings whose recorded altitude differs from the tracked one by more than this (a lost bottom lock that still writes a value).

None min_altitude_m float

Detection ignores samples nearer than this.

0.5 min_return_m float

Slant distance the return must stay above threshold, converted to samples and used as the detector's min_run when longer. A transmit burst (some recorders keep it; it can start after a quiet lead-in and be as bright as the seabed) lasts a metre or two; the seabed return lasts tens of metres.

5.0 min_return_fraction float

Fraction of that distance that must be above threshold (min_run_fraction of the detector), so shadows and gaps in a rough seabed return do not push the onset further out.

0.7 smooth_window int

Passed to :func:detect_first_bottom_return (min_run in samples, raised to min_return_m when that is longer).

10 threshold_fraction int

Passed to :func:detect_first_bottom_return (min_run in samples, raised to min_return_m when that is longer).

10 min_run int

Passed to :func:detect_first_bottom_return (min_run in samples, raised to min_return_m when that is longer).

10 smooth_pings int

Rolling median of the tracked altitude over this many pings (:func:smooth_boundary_across_pings); 1 = none. Smoothing looks across pings, so a chunked :func:~sidescanpy.processing.correct_file run can differ from an unchunked one within smooth_pings // 2 pings of each chunk edge.

1

Returns:

Type Description Dataset

ds with altitude_m replaced where selected and a "bottom_track" history record. Pings with no detection keep their recorded value. fathometer_reading_m is not changed.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.correct
docs.text:
One correction API: apply an ordered list of steps, each skippable and replaceable, recording every applied step in processing_history.

  • :func:correct -- one frequency channel dataset.
  • :func:correct_survey -- every channel of a survey (supplies the survey's aux records to the "interpolate_aux" step).
  • :func:correct_file -- read a .ss.h5 file, correct it, write it atomically (in place by default), optionally in ping chunks to bound memory.
  • :func:correction_steps -- a set of requested built-in steps in canonical order, with "interpolate_aux" added when a step needs it.
Steps

A step is a built-in name, a :class:Step (custom name + function) or any callable fn(ds, **params) -> ds. Built-in steps, in canonical order:

"crop_farrange" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.farrange.crop_far_range. Params: cutoff_sample, n_bins, min_valid_fraction, rise_threshold_db, margin_bins. "interpolate_aux" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.interpolate.interpolate_aux_onto_dataset; needs the survey's aux records (aux= / :func:correct_survey); :func:correct skips it when no aux is given. Params: fields, method, extrapolation, drop_invalid, held_values, max_hold_s, per_ping_fallback, groups, merge_window_s. "bottom_track" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.bottom.altitude_from_bottom_track: set altitude_m from the first bottom return where it is missing (NaN or <= 0), before the geometric step needs it. Not in :data:DEFAULT_STEPS. Params: replace, max_diff_m, min_altitude_m, min_return_m, min_return_fraction, smooth_window, threshold_fraction, min_run, smooth_pings. "tvg" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.radiometric.apply_tvg. Params: spreading_loss_db, absorption_db_per_m, min_range_m, sound_velocity_ms, plus temperature_c, salinity_psu, depth_m, ph (Francois-Garrison inputs, used only when absorption_db_per_m is None; model of Francois & Garrison, J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(3) 896-907 and 72(6) 1879-1890, 1982). "geometric" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.geometric.compute_geometric_ranges. Params: expose_unmasked_z. "range_correction" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.range_correction.apply_empirical_range_correction (needs tvg + geometric). Params: table (required: a RangeCorrectionTable or the path of a saved one; no built-in default). "georef" :func:~sidescanpy.processing.georeferencing.compute_georeferencing (needs geometric). Params: ellipsoid.

Steps run in the order given; dependencies are the caller's to respect. :data:DEFAULT_STEPS is interpolate_aux -> tvg -> geometric -> georef.

Conventions
  • Skip a step by leaving it out of steps. params may only name steps that are in steps (a typo raises ValueError); a parameter the step does not accept raises TypeError. Both are checked before anything runs.
  • Idempotent: a step already applied (see :func:sidescanpy.core.history.has_step) is skipped with a DEBUG log, so re-running is a no-op. Custom steps are matched by name, so give each one a distinct name (lambdas are rejected for that reason).
  • force=True re-applies already-applied steps. A radiometric step (tvg/range_correction) is first inverted -- together with every radiometric step applied after it, all of which must then be in steps -- so its new parameters replace, not stack on, the old ones.
  • History: every applied step appends one record {"step", "params", "function", "version", "timestamp_utc"} with the parameters actually used (defaults resolved). Built-in steps write their own record; custom steps are recorded here with the bound arguments.
  • No uncorrected copy is kept: :func:sidescanpy.processing.inversion.invert undoes recorded steps.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.farrange
docs.text:
Far-range noise detection and cropping.

Some surveys record a channel's sample window well past where real backscatter decays into noise — a per-survey acquisition setting, not fixed by frequency. Past that point, raw amplitude doesn't stay flat — it climbs back up, new evidence for a hardware TVG/AGC artifact baked into the raw signal — which apply_tvg()'s uncapped, monotonically-increasing gain formula then massively over-amplifies (a ~57 dB overshoot measured on real data), saturating percentile-based color scales and burying the real near-nadir signal. This module detects that decay-then-rise pattern directly from the uncorrected signal (and crops it out — intentionally conservative: a channel with no detected rise is left untouched, not cropped by a guessed constant, since the recorded window length varies per survey.

Binning is done by raw sample index, not real range — this needs no geometric computation (no aux interpolation, no altitude), so it can run immediately after conversion, before any other correction step.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: detect_far_range_cutoff_sample
docs.text:
detect_far_range_cutoff_sample(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    n_bins: int = 40,
    min_valid_fraction: float = 0.5,
    rise_threshold_db: float = 3.0,
    margin_bins: int = 1,
) -> int | None

Detect the sample index beyond which backscatter climbs back up after decaying into its real noise floor.

Works on the uncorrected signal: any recorded radiometric steps are inverted first (:func:sidescanpy.processing.inversion.uncorrected_backscatter), so it can run before or after TVG. Bin statistics are accumulated in ping blocks, so memory stays bounded on large (or dask-backed) datasets.

Bins the uncorrected signal (converted to dB) by sample index across n_bins roughly-equal bins, finds the peak bin (the strongest mean return) among bins with enough finite samples to be statistically reliable, then finds the minimum-mean bin after that peak (the real far-range floor — searched only post-peak so a legitimate near-nadir ramp-up is never mistaken for the floor). If any later, equally-reliable bin's mean then rises rise_threshold_db or more above that floor, returns a cropped sample count (the floor bin's end, plus margin_bins of slack). If no such rise is found, returns None — nothing should be cropped.

A cutoff whose slant range is not beyond the median altitude_m is rejected with a WARNING and None is returned: on recordings that include the transmit pulse and the water column, the "floor" found is the water column and the "rise" is the seafloor return.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

A single frequency channel dataset.

required n_bins int

Number of sample-index bins to divide the sample axis into.

40 min_valid_fraction float

A bin is "reliable" only if at least this fraction of its n_pings * n_channels * bin_size cells are finite.

0.5 rise_threshold_db float

How far above the detected floor a later, reliable bin's mean must climb to count as "the noise climbing back up".

3.0 margin_bins int

Extra bins kept past the detected floor bin.

1

Returns:

Type Description int or None

Sample count to crop to (ds.isel(sample=slice(0, result))), or None if no crop is warranted.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.geometric
docs.text:
Geometric range computation for SideScan sonar data.

Computes per-sample geometric variables as data variables attached to the dataset. Does NOT resample backscatter — original sample positions and values are preserved. Downstream tools (xarray.interp, rioxarray, etc.) handle resampling onto regular grids on demand.

Outputs (all shape (ping, channel, sample)): slant_range_m attitude-invariant time-of-flight range ground_range_m sqrt(slant^2 - altitude^2), unsigned (flat-bottom, no pitch correction) across_track_m signed Y component, pitch-corrected (negative = port, positive = starboard) along_track_m signed X component, pitch-induced offset (positive = forward of nadir, negative = aft) vertical_offset_m Z component from platform = altitude_m for flat bottom (broadcast). Future: extends to bathymetry. depth_per_sample_m absolute water depth at sample location = depth_m + altitude_m

Sign conventions: - across_track_m: port channel negative, starboard positive - along_track_m: positive forward of nadir (pitch-up reflects forward)

Pitch-correction math: across_track_m = ±ground_range_m * cos(pitch_rad) along_track_m = +ground_range_m * sin(pitch_rad)

Roll's effect on altitude is intentionally not modeled here. Future work: when DVL altitude is available it's pre-corrected; when only fathometer_reading_m is available, attitude correction is applied to derive altitude_m.

processing_history is appended with a "geometric" record.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: compute_geometric_ranges
docs.text:
compute_geometric_ranges(
    ds: Dataset, *, expose_unmasked_z: bool = False
) -> xr.Dataset

Attach per-sample geometric variables to the dataset.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

Validated sidescan dataset.

required expose_unmasked_z bool

If True, vertical_offset_m and depth_per_sample_m are written as per-ping values broadcast to (ping, channel, sample) without masking the water column. The Z-axis variables become well-defined per-ping constants for every sample. The default (False) masks them with the same NaN mask as ground_range_m for consistency.

False

Returns:

New dataset (input not modified) with six added per-sample data variables and a "geometric" processing_history record.

Notes

NaN handling: - NaN altitude_m for a ping → all per-sample geometry NaN for that ping (slant_range_m is unaffected; it's altitude-independent). - NaN sound_vel_ms for a ping → falls back to 1500 m/s with warning. - Water-column samples (slant <= altitude) → NaN in ground_range_m, across_track_m, along_track_m, and (by default) vertical_offset_m and depth_per_sample_m.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.georeferencing
docs.text:
Per-sample georeferencing: compute latitude_per_sample and longitude_per_sample from per-ping nav, heading, and the platform-frame offsets (across_track_m, along_track_m) attached by compute_geometric_ranges.

Uses pyproj.Geod for geodetic forward calculations on a specified ellipsoid (WGS84 by default). Vectorized over the entire (ping, channel, sample) array via a single Geod.fwd call.

Bearing convention: compass heading (north = 0, increasing clockwise). Per-sample bearing is heading + atan2(across_track, along_track).

NaN propagation: - Any NaN per-ping latitude, longitude, or heading → all samples for that ping are NaN. - Any NaN per-sample across_track or along_track → that sample is NaN.

processing_history is appended with a "georef" record.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.interpolate
docs.text:
Interpolate auxiliary records onto per-ping timestamps.

The converter populates per-ping fields (latitude, heading_deg, etc.) on each SideScanFrequencyChannel from the embedded values in SonarDataMessage. For many quantities those embedded values are stale — they're the most-recent auxiliary reading at the moment the ping was recorded, not interpolated to the ping's exact timestamp.

This module provides higher-precision per-ping values by interpolating each frequency channel's ping times against the survey's auxiliary records.

Aux records are themselves often sample-and-hold (each entry repeats the latest sensor value until the sensor updates). By default (held_values="fixes") each record is first reduced to its real fixes with :func:~sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes.held_value_fixes, so the interpolated track is smooth instead of stair-stepped. When a field has no usable aux source, the channel's own per-ping values (also typically held) are reduced the same way and interpolated (per_ping_fallback).

Two layers:

  • interpolate_aux_onto_pings(survey, ...) — top-level entrypoint. Iterates the default field-to-aux mapping (or a user override) and applies interpolation per channel.

  • interpolate_onto_channel(channel, source, field_map, ...) — lower level. Takes any xr.Dataset with a time coordinate as the source, enabling external data (e.g. a separately recorded GPS log) to drive per-ping field updates.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: interpolate_aux_onto_pings
docs.text:
interpolate_aux_onto_pings(
    survey: SideScanSurvey,
    *,
    fields: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
    method: str = "linear",
    extrapolation: Literal[
        "clamp", "linear", "nan"
    ] = "clamp",
    drop_invalid: bool = True,
    force: bool = False,
    in_place: bool = False,
    held_values: Literal["fixes", "raw"] = "fixes",
    max_hold_s: float = 2.0,
    per_ping_fallback: bool = True,
    groups: Sequence[Sequence[str]] | None = None,
    merge_window_s: MergeWindow = None,
) -> SideScanSurvey

Update per-ping fields on every frequency channel by interpolating the survey's auxiliary records onto each ping's timestamp.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default survey SideScanSurvey

Survey to operate on.

required fields dict

Mapping {per_ping_field: (aux_name, aux_var)}. Overrides the default in DEFAULT_FIELD_SOURCES. Use this to interpolate only a subset of fields, or to point a field at a non-default source.

None method str

Interpolation method passed to xarray.Dataset.interp — "linear", "nearest", "cubic", etc.

"linear" extrapolation (clamp, linear, nan)

Behavior when a ping's timestamp falls outside the aux record's time range. "clamp" holds the boundary value; "linear" extrapolates the slope; "nan" writes NaN.

"clamp" drop_invalid bool

If True, drop rows where the aux source variable is NaN before interpolating. Avoids NaN propagation through the interpolated result. Set False to require the source be clean. With held_values="fixes" NaN entries are never fixes and are always dropped.

True force bool

If True, attempt interpolation even when the aux record is empty or absent and no per-ping fallback applies: the per-ping field receives NaN. If False (default), the field is left unchanged and a warning is logged.

False in_place bool

If True, mutate survey in place and return it. If False, return a new SideScanSurvey leaving the input untouched.

False held_values (fixes, raw)

"fixes" reduces each aux record to its real fixes first (:func:~sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes.held_value_fixes): many recorders log the latest GPS or attitude value at every ping or packet, and interpolating between those repeated entries keeps the stair-steps (consecutive pings stack on one position, then jump). "raw" interpolates the entries as logged (the only behavior up to 0.7.2).

"fixes" max_hold_s float

With held_values="fixes": a value unchanged for longer than this is kept flat across the hold (a stop, or a sensor dropout) rather than ramped through it. See :func:~sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes.held_value_fixes.

2.0 per_ping_fallback bool

With held_values="fixes": when a field's aux record is absent or empty, or its variable is missing or all NaN, reduce the channel's own per-ping values of that field (against the ping times) to fixes and interpolate those instead. Per-ping values that never repeat are returned unchanged. The fields filled this way are recorded in the history entry. No effect with held_values="raw".

True groups sequence of sequence of str

With held_values="fixes": variables that update together, passed to :func:~sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes.held_value_fixes for each record (by aux variable name; for the per-ping fallback, by per-ping field name). A group applies to a record only when all its variables are in it, so groups=[POSITION_GROUP] joins latitude and longitude in the navigation record and leaves attitude alone. Default: every variable is its own group.

None merge_window_s float or mapping of str to float

With held_values="fixes": merge changes at most this many seconds apart into one update event, for recorders that log one sensor update over consecutive entries. A float applies to every group of every record; a mapping by aux variable name (for the per-ping fallback, by per-ping field name), such as {"latitude": 0.15, "longitude": 0.15}, only to those variables' groups. See :func:~sidescanpy.processing.aux_fixes.held_value_fixes. Default None: no merging.

None

Returns:

Type Description SideScanSurvey

Survey with updated per-ping fields. Each touched frequency channel gets a new processing_history entry.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If fields references an unknown aux record name. If extrapolation or held_values is not one of the supported values, or max_hold_s or merge_window_s is out of range.

docs.text:
interpolate_aux_onto_dataset(
    ds: Dataset,
    aux: SideScanSurvey,
    *,
    fields: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] | None = None,
    method: str = "linear",
    extrapolation: Literal[
        "clamp", "linear", "nan"
    ] = "clamp",
    drop_invalid: bool = True,
    force: bool = False,
    held_values: Literal["fixes", "raw"] = "fixes",
    max_hold_s: float = 2.0,
    per_ping_fallback: bool = True,
    groups: Sequence[Sequence[str]] | None = None,
    merge_window_s: MergeWindow = None,

One frequency channel dataset's per-ping fields, interpolated from aux's auxiliary records (the "interpolate_aux" step).

Same parameters as :func:interpolate_aux_onto_pings, but for a single dataset (or a ping slice of one) with the survey supplying the aux records. Always appends an "interpolate_aux" history record (with the fields actually updated, possibly none, held_values, max_hold_s, per_ping_fallback, groups, merge_window_s and the fields filled from per-ping values as per_ping_fallback_fields) so the step is not re-run.

For the per-ping fallback on a ping slice, the per-ping values come from the matching whole channel in aux (same freq_hz_start, same times at the slice's ping coordinates) when there is one, so a chunked run gives the same result as an unchunked one.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.inversion
docs.text:
Undo recorded corrections, driven by processing_history.

No uncorrected copy of the backscatter is stored: radiometric steps are inverted exactly from the parameters recorded in their history records, and geometric/georef steps are undone by dropping the variables they added.

  • :func:uncorrected_backscatter -- the pre-radiometric signal as a DataArray (nothing else touched). Works lazily on dask-backed data.
  • :func:invert -- a dataset with the chosen steps undone and their history records removed.

Not invertible: crop_farrange (samples are gone), interpolate_aux (the converter's embedded per-ping values were overwritten) and caller-supplied steps (unknown effect).

Legacy files: TVG records written by older versions (tvg_correction) carry the same parameters and invert the same way. A legacy file whose only TVG evidence is the processing_level == "radiometric" attribute falls back to its stored LEGACY_RAW_VAR (backscatter_raw) variable.

invert(
    ds: Dataset, steps: Iterable[str] | None = None

Undo recorded correction steps.

Parameters:

Frequency channel dataset.

required steps iterable of str

Steps to undo, any of :data:INVERTIBLE_STEPS. Default: every one that has been applied. Radiometric steps are undone newest first and must include every radiometric step recorded after the oldest one requested (tvg cannot be undone underneath a later range_correction). Undoing geometric also undoes georef (it is derived from the geometric variables) and requires range_correction to be undone too if it was applied (it needs ground_range_m). docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.navigation
docs.text:
Navigation-derived ping geometry: along-track distance and nav-stall repair.

  • :func:along_track_distance_m -- cumulative along-track distance (m) from per-ping latitude/longitude, optionally with short navigation stalls filled.
  • :func:fill_nav_stalls -- replace short runs of stalled position steps with the local median ping step.

Pure array/dataset functions; no plotting.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: along_track_distance_m
docs.text:
along_track_distance_m(
    ds: Dataset, *, fill_nav_stalls: bool = False
) -> np.ndarray

Cumulative along-track distance (meters) from per-ping lat/lon.

Public wrapper around the same computation used internally for y_axis="along_track" — exposed for callers (e.g. distance-based segmentation) that need the coordinate array without going through plot_waterfall.

fill_nav_stalls: navigation can stall -- several consecutive pings keep (nearly) the same position while the vessel keeps moving, and it resumes without catching up. The raw distance is then flat across those pings, and geometric resampling stacks their seafloor into a single along-track line (seen on one real survey: ~7 pings at each checked target, 42ms apart with distinct data, advanced only ~0.07m in total instead of ~0.5m -- a hard seam through the target at fine resolution). With True, each stalled step is replaced by the local median step (see fill_nav_stalls). Off by default so gap/stationarity detection still sees the raw navigation.

docs.title: fill_nav_stalls
docs.text:
fill_nav_stalls(
    along: ndarray,
    *,
    stall_fraction: float = 0.5,
    max_stall_pings: int = 20,
    window_pings: int = 25,
) -> np.ndarray

Replace short navigation stalls with the local median ping step.

A step is stalled when it is below stall_fraction of the median step within window_pings either side. Only runs of at most max_stall_pings stalled steps with moving steps on both sides are filled -- a longer run, or one at the window edge, is treated as the vessel really stopping and left as is.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.outliers
docs.text:
Median/MAD outlier rejection.

:func:reject_range_outliers drops samples far from their own range bin's median. Meant for calibration-style fits that assume a flat, homogeneous bottom population (noise-floor and range-decay estimates), not for display or export: it deliberately discards genuine bright returns such as hard targets.

:func:mask_bright_ping_rows drops whole pings whose overall level is an outlier -- the full-width bright streak a per-ping automatic gain jump leaves.

docs.title: reject_range_outliers
docs.text:
reject_range_outliers(
    values: ndarray,
    ranges: ndarray,
    *,
    bin_width_m: float = 5.0,
    mad_k: float = 3.5,
    min_bin_count: int = 5,
) -> np.ndarray

Return a copy of values with per-range-bin outliers set to NaN.

Samples are grouped into bin_width_m range bins; within each bin a sample is rejected when its modified z-score 0.6745 * |value - median| / MAD exceeds mad_k. Median/MAD rather than mean/std, so the right-skewed backscatter distribution doesn't hide the outliers it contains.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default values ndarray

Same shape, any dims (flattened internally, reshaped on return).

required ranges ndarray

Same shape, any dims (flattened internally, reshaped on return).

required bin_width_m float

docs.text:
mask_bright_ping_rows(
    array_2d: ndarray, mad_k: float = 3.5
) -> np.ndarray

NaN out whole ping rows whose typical level is an extreme outlier.

Hardware with per-ping automatic gain control occasionally raises one ping's gain well above its neighbors, leaving a uniformly bright, full-width streak. The gain multiplies the whole ping, so clipping values only dims the streak; masking the row removes it. Each row's level is its median; a row is masked when its modified z-score 0.6745 * |level - median| / MAD across rows exceeds mad_k.

(n_pings, n_samples).

3.5

array_2d itself when nothing is masked (or fewer than 5 rows have a finite level, or the MAD is 0), otherwise a copy with the outlier rows NaN.
