docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.radiometric
docs.text:
Radiometric correction for sidescan sonar data.

This module implements Time-Varying Gain (TVG) correction to compensate for transmission losses in the water column. The raw backscatter_intensity values represent echo levels received by the transducer but do not account for:

  1. Geometric spreading: sound spreads in 3D, so intensity falls as 1/R² each way. Over the two-way path that is 40log10(R) dB (samples are amplitude, converted with 20log10, so dB values are comparable to intensity dB). Some authors use 30log10(R) for sidescan, because the insonified seafloor patch grows in proportion to R and adds back 10log10(R) (see the note on :class:TVGParams); the coefficient is a parameter, not fixed.
  2. Absorption: water absorbs acoustic energy proportional to distance traveled (in dB: 2alphaR dB loss for two-way path)

TVG correction adds these losses back, so equal backscatter at different ranges produces equal corrected values. This is essential for radiometric calibration and mosaic generation.

The default absorption coefficient comes from the Francois-Garrison seawater absorption model (:func:francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m):

  • R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part I: Pure water and magnesium sulfate contributions," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(3), 896-907 (1982).
  • R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part II: Boric acid contribution and equation for total absorption," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(6), 1879-1890 (1982).

Input backscatter is assumed to be linear amplitude; this module converts to dB, applies TVG, and outputs dB. The step is recorded in processing_history with its resolved parameters so it can be inverted exactly.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: DEFAULT_SPREADING_LOSS_DB module-attribute
docs.text:
DEFAULT_SPREADING_LOSS_DB = 30.0

Default TVG spreading coefficient (dB per decade of range): 30 log R.

Used by :class:TVGParams and the TVG curve fits. 30 log R models the insonified seafloor area growing with range; 40 log R (two-way spherical spreading) and 20 log R (one-way) remain available by passing spreading_loss_db.

docs.title: TVGParams dataclass
docs.text:
Parameters for time-varying gain correction.

Attributes:

Name Type Description spreading_loss_db float, default=30.0

Spreading loss coefficient (dB per decade of range): the gain is spreading_loss_db * log10(R). 30.0 (the default, :data:DEFAULT_SPREADING_LOSS_DB) models the insonified seafloor area growing with range (e.g. J. Mar. Sci. Eng. 2017, 5(4), 54, https://www.mdpi.com/2077-1312/5/4/54). 40.0 is two-way spherical spreading (the default in 0.7.0-0.7.5); 20.0 is one-way spherical spreading (the default before 0.7.0). Which fits real data varies, so measure with :func:sidescanpy.analysis.fit_range_decay per survey. 0.0 disables the term (hardware already compensates spreading).

absorption_db_per_m (float, optional)

Absorption coefficient (dB per meter). If None, derived from the channel frequency with :func:francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m (Francois & Garrison, J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(3) 896-907 and 72(6) 1879-1890, 1982) and the four water parameters below (typical-coastal defaults where None).

min_range_m float, default=0.5

Minimum range threshold (meters). Ranges below this are clipped to avoid log(0) singularity. Typical value 0.5 m accounts for transducer blanking.

sound_velocity_ms (float, optional)

Sound velocity (m/s) used to turn sample index into slant range. If None, the mean of the dataset's per-ping sound_vel_ms.

temperature_c, salinity_psu, depth_m, ph (float, optional)

Water conditions for the Francois-Garrison absorption; used only when absorption_db_per_m is None (defaults 10 C, 35 psu, 10 m, pH 8 -- pass real values when known).

docs.title: francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m
docs.text:
francois_garrison_absorption_db_per_m(
    frequency_hz,
    *,
    temperature_c: float = DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_C,
    salinity_psu: float = DEFAULT_SALINITY_PSU,
    depth_m: float = DEFAULT_DEPTH_M,
    ph: float = DEFAULT_PH,
    sound_velocity_ms: float | None = None,
)

Seawater sound absorption (dB/m, one-way) after Francois & Garrison (1982).

Sum of three relaxation / viscosity terms (f in kHz, result in dB/km before conversion)::

alpha = A1 P1 f1 f^2 / (f1^2 + f^2)      boric acid
      + A2 P2 f2 f^2 / (f2^2 + f^2)      magnesium sulfate
      + A3 P3 f^2                        pure water (viscosity)

with the paper's coefficients: f1 = 2.8 sqrt(S/35) 10^(4 - 1245/(T+273)), f2 = 8.17 10^(8 - 1990/(T+273)) / (1 + 0.0018 (S - 35)), A3 having separate polynomial branches for T <= 20 C and T > 20 C, and depth factors P2, P3. Valid roughly 0.4 - 1000 kHz, -1.8 to 30 C, S 30-35 psu, depth 0 - 6 km.

References

.. [1] R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part I: Pure water and magnesium sulfate contributions," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(3), 896-907 (1982) (pure water and magnesium sulfate terms). .. [2] R. E. Francois and G. R. Garrison, "Sound absorption based on ocean measurements: Part II: Boric acid contribution and equation for total absorption," J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 72(6), 1879-1890 (1982) (boric acid term and the equation for total absorption).

The defaults are "typical coastal" values (10 C, 35 psu, 10 m, pH 8), not a measurement: callers with real conditions should pass their own.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default frequency_hz float or array_like

Frequency (Hz). Vectorised.

required temperature_c float

Water conditions (degrees C, practical salinity units, metres, pH).

DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_C salinity_psu float

Water conditions (degrees C, practical salinity units, metres, pH).

DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_C depth_m float

Water conditions (degrees C, practical salinity units, metres, pH).

DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_C ph float

Water conditions (degrees C, practical salinity units, metres, pH).

DEFAULT_TEMPERATURE_C sound_velocity_ms float

Sound speed (m/s) in the relaxation-amplitude terms. Default: the paper's own c = 1412 + 3.21 T + 1.19 S + 0.0167 D.

None

Returns:

Type Description float or ndarray

Absorption coefficient in dB per metre (the paper's dB/km / 1000), a float for scalar input.

docs.title: tvg_gain_db
docs.text:
tvg_gain_db(
    range_m: ndarray, params: TVGParams
) -> np.ndarray

Per-range TVG gain (dB): spreading loss + absorption loss.

spreading_loss (dB) = spreading_loss_db * log10(range_m) absorption_loss (dB) = 2 * absorption_db_per_m * range_m (factor of 2 for the two-way path)

Shared by apply_tvg() (xarray survey pipeline) and apply_tvg_to_amplitude() (plain-array path, e.g. target crop windows) so both apply the identical formula rather than maintaining it twice. Caller is responsible for clipping range_m to params.min_range_m first (as both callers here do) — this function doesn't clip on its own since it has no opinion on what a caller's minimum range should be.

For use on data that isn't a full survey channel (e.g. a target's raw ping-sample window decoded straight from its catalog SQLite via sidescanpy.io.jsf.targets.decode_target_window), where constructing a full SideScanSurvey/Dataset just to TVG-correct a small crop isn't warranted. Range covered by one sample (two-way), e.g. a target catalog's own PingMetersPerSample — the per-sample analog of apply_tvg()'s sound_velocity / (2 * sample_rate).

If None, built from defaults with absorption_db_per_m derived from freq_hz (required in that case, matching apply_tvg()'s own default-resolution pattern).

docs.title: apply_tvg
docs.text:
apply_tvg(
    ds: Dataset, params: TVGParams | None = None
) -> xr.Dataset

Apply time-varying gain (TVG) correction to backscatter_intensity.

Compensates for geometric spreading and acoustic absorption losses. Converts linear amplitude to dB (20*log10(clip(x, 1e-6)), see :mod:sidescanpy.core.units), adds the TVG gain for each sample's slant range, and returns corrected dB values in place of the input.

Input backscatter_intensity is assumed to be linear amplitude; the library does not check this (what units the input data is in is the caller's knowledge). Exact-zero amplitude maps to the -120 dB floor.

The step is recorded in processing_history as "tvg" with the parameters actually used (defaults resolved), which is what :func:sidescanpy.processing.correct.invert reads to undo it.

Frequency channel dataset; needs backscatter_intensity, sound_vel_ms and the freq_hz_start/sample_rate_hz attrs.

required params TVGParams

If None, defaults with absorption_db_per_m derived from freq_hz_start and sound_velocity_ms from the mean per-ping sound_vel_ms. The caller's object is never modified.

None

Returns:

New dataset with TVG-corrected dB backscatter_intensity and the "tvg" history record appended.

If TVG has already been applied (prevents double application).

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.range_correction
docs.text:
Empirical range correction for the residual TVG range-dependence.

processing/radiometric.py's apply_tvg() implements the physically- grounded spreading+absorption TVG model. Even after that model is applied real data can show a remaining, altitude-invariant, non-monotonic range-dependent residual. This module does not attempt to model the physical cause (it is not a mistuned absorption coefficient or a missing grazing-angle/beam-pattern correction). Instead it fits and removes whatever range-dependent shape is actually observed in TVG-corrected data, per frequency.

The library ships no calibration table: a table is fit from a specific survey and instrument, so it belongs with the project that fitted it. Fit one with :func:fit_range_correction, store it with :meth:RangeCorrectionTable.save, and pass it (or its path) as the table argument of :func:apply_empirical_range_correction / the "range_correction" step.

This is a separate, optional correction step ("range_correction") from apply_tvg() — not in sidescanpy.processing.DEFAULT_STEPS; opt in by listing it in the steps passed to sidescanpy.processing.correct.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: RangeCorrectionTable
docs.text:
Per-frequency empirical range-correction lookup.

Each calibrated frequency stores a piecewise-linear correction curve (range-bin centers -> correction_db) fit by :func:fit_range_correction. This is the "non-parametric smooth interpolation over the observed bins" approach from the design doc — deliberately not a fitted polynomial, since the two frequencies calibrated so far have qualitatively different residual shapes (a smooth bowl vs. a sharp near-field rise-then-plateau) that a low-order polynomial risks fitting poorly or overfitting.

docs.title: correction_db_at
docs.text:
correction_db_at(
    freq_hz: float,
    range_m: ndarray,
    tolerance_hz: float = _FREQ_MATCH_TOLERANCE_HZ,
) -> np.ndarray | None

Evaluate the fitted correction curve for freq_hz at range_m.

Piecewise-linear interpolation between calibrated range-bin centers. range_m values outside the calibration data's observed span are clamped to the nearest edge's correction value (np.interp's default constant-extrapolation behavior) — a deliberate, documented policy, not an accident: the calibration data doesn't cover ranges never seen in the fitting survey, and clamping is the safest default versus extrapolating an unverified shape.

docs.text:
fit_range_correction(
    ds: Dataset,
    bin_width_m: float = 5.0,
    exclude_below_db: float | None = -110.0,
) -> tuple[list[float], list[float], dict]

Fit an empirical range-correction curve from one TVG-corrected channel.

Must be TVG-corrected and have a ground_range_m variable — i.e. already run through the "tvg" and "geometric" steps.

Passed through to processing.profiles.backscatter_vs_range.

5.0 exclude_below_db float

Passed through as exclude_below_db to exclude the floor-clipped samples (~-120 dB exact-zero-amplitude floor) from biasing the fit. None disables filtering.

range_m/correction_db are bin-center arrays ready for RangeCorrectionTable.add_curve(). correction_db[i] is defined as target_level_db - mean_backscatter[i], where target_level_db is the count-weighted mean across all bins — i.e. the fitted correction has ~zero net effect on the survey's average absolute level, it only flattens the range-dependent shape.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.segments
docs.text:
Survey segmentation: find clean, homogeneous ping ranges in one channel.

Aggregate analysis over a ping range that silently mixes a gap, a setting change, a dropout or a turn transient gives misleading numbers. These detectors find such stretches so they can be cut out first.

  • :func:detect_gaps — along-track distance or ping-time jumps.
  • :func:detect_setting_changes — valid_samples or sound-velocity steps.
  • :func:detect_garbage_runs — sustained runs of all-NaN/zero pings.
  • :func:detect_unstable_spans — altitude/pitch instability windows (scored by :func:score_stability).

:func:find_segments combines them into :class:Segment objects labelled "clean" or "excluded" with the reasons that fired. :func:split_by_segments slices a survey into one sub-survey per clean segment; :func:write_segments writes each to its own .ss.h5.

docs.text:
detect_gaps(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    gap_factor: float = 8.0,
    time_gap_factor: float = 8.0,
) -> np.ndarray

Per-ping boundary flags: True at i marks a break between pings i-1 and i.

Fires when the along-track step exceeds gap_factor times the median nonzero step, or the ping-time step exceeds time_gap_factor times the median nonzero interval. Either signal alone can show a real discontinuity. Index 0 is never flagged.

docs.text:
score_stability(
    altitude: ndarray, pitch: ndarray, start: int, span: int
) -> float

Stability score of [start, start + span); lower is calmer.

Altitude coefficient of variation plus pitch standard deviation (degrees), weighted 1:1. A calm stretch scores a few hundredths to tenths; a turn or deployment transient scores one to two orders of magnitude higher. inf with fewer than two finite values.

[(start, stop), ...] unstable stretches from altitude and pitch.

Non-overlapping window_pings windows scoring above stability_threshold (:func:score_stability) are unstable; adjacent ones merge, and a merged span shorter than min_run_pings is dropped as noise. The default threshold is a coarse starting point, not a validated value. Empty without altitude_m and pitch_deg.

    stability_window_pings: int = 100,
    stability_threshold: float = 1.0,
    stability_min_run_pings: int = 50,
    min_segment_pings: int = 200,
) -> list[Segment]

Split [0, n_pings) into contiguous :class:Segment objects.

Gap and setting-change flags become boundaries; garbage and unstable spans become "excluded" segments. Each segment's reasons names every signal that fired inside it (["clean"] if none).

Status is resolved per raw interval before merging. Only a clean interval shorter than min_segment_pings is merged, and only into a preceding clean neighbour, so a short excluded span never taints clean pings. A short clean interval with no clean neighbour is kept as is.

docs.title: sidescanpy.processing.slicing
docs.text:
Slicing operations for SideScan frequency channels.

Every function takes an xr.Dataset (one frequency channel) and returns a new xr.Dataset -- the sliced version of the input. Empty slices (zero pings or zero samples) are valid and return an empty-but- schema-valid dataset. slice_survey maps any of them over every frequency of a SideScanSurvey.

Slicing is structural: backscatter values, processing_level, and processing_history are preserved. No values are modified.

Available slicing functions:

  • slice_by_pings — by ping index range
  • ping_windows — (start, stop) ranges tiling a ping axis, for windowed reads
  • slice_by_samples — by absolute sample coordinate range
  • slice_by_range — by slant range in metres
  • slice_by_time — by ping timestamp range (supports str or datetime64)
  • slice_by_bbox — by lat/lon bounding box (per-ping by default, per-sample with use_per_sample=True)
  • slice_by_ground_range — by maximum ground range (requires ground_range_m to be present, run compute_geometric_ranges first)

docs.title: build_survey_track
docs.text:
build_survey_track(
    surveys: dict, freq_key: str, *, scanline_stride: int
) -> Optional[SurveyTrack]

Nadir track + strided port/starboard scan-line endpoints for one frequency, across every file that has it, in time order.

Cheap by design, but not by slicing the sample axis down to one sample before georeferencing — that's tempting (we only want the farthest-range sample per ping) but wrong: compute_geometric_ranges computes each sample's position from the absolute sample coordinate when present (processing.sample_axis. sample_index), so slicing samples is safe for datasets that carry it. For legacy datasets without that coordinate it falls back to a local index (arange(ds.sizes["sample"])): pre-slicing to sample=[-1] then makes the function see "sample 0" (point-blank range) instead of the true far-range edge — silently producing NaN via the water-column mask instead of a real position.

The safe optimization instead pre-selects the strided pings (slicing the ping axis doesn't touch ds.sizes["sample"], so it doesn't affect the sample-index math) while keeping each selected ping's full sample axis intact through georeferencing, and only slices to the last sample afterward. This still avoids georeferencing every ping — just the ones actually needed for a rung — while staying correct.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default surveys dict[Path, SideScanSurvey] required freq_key str

e.g. "hz_1495000".

required scanline_stride int

Draw a scan-line rung every Nth ping.

required

Returns:

Type Description SurveyTrack or None

None if no file has freq_key. Track arrays cover every ping; scan arrays cover every scanline_stride-th ping.

docs.title: sidescanpy.targets
docs.text:
Format-agnostic sonar target/contact model.

A Target describes one sonar contact/pick, which may carry position information in either (or both) of two address spaces: native (ping/channel/sample, lat/lon — how a survey's own target catalog describes it) and pixel (image id + bbox — how ML interchange formats like COCO/YOLO describe it).

The data model itself lives in :mod:sidescanpy.core.target (re-exported here). Format-specific catalog readers live next to that format's other IO code (e.g. sidescanpy.io.jsf.targets); this package holds target JSON/CSV IO, window decoding and display helpers, and position correlation against converted surveys. ML annotation writers (COCO/YOLO) are in :mod:sidescanpy.export.ml.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: sidescanpy.targets.correlate
docs.text:
Resolve target positions and clock offsets against converted .ss.h5 files.

Catalog formats that store no absolute position (the Klein .tgt reader in :mod:sidescanpy.io.sdf.targets) are located here against per-ping times of converted surveys. For Klein catalogs use :func:resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping, which matches the catalog's own ping time and number exactly; the pick-timestamp functions (with optional constant clock-offset calibration) match the later save time and are only a fallback for catalogs without those fields. Also provides position-based correlation of any target to a ping in a directory of converted surveys, and projection of a target onto another frequency channel.

    ss_h5_dir: str | Path, *, local_utc_offset_hours: float

Filenames are expected to embed <YYMMDD><HHMMSS> local start time (matches Klein SDF's own sonar_data<YYMMDD><HHMMSS>.sdf naming, preserved through conversion). Enriches each matched target with altitude_m/speed_mps/ meters_per_ping/ground_range_m in extra_attributes — all approximations from the nearest matched ping, not per-sample measurements, and constant across a target's ~256-ping window. position_confidence stays "unknown" regardless of match quality, matching :func:resolve_target_position's convention. docs.title: resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping
docs.text:
resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping(
    targets: list[Target],
    ss_h5_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    max_time_delta_s: float = 1.5,
) -> list[Target]

Place targets at the ping their catalog names (Klein .tgt).

Klein catalogs store the target ping's own time and ping number (extra_attributes["catalog_ping_time"] / ["catalog_ping_number"], see :mod:sidescanpy.io.sdf.targets) on the sonar's clock, the same clock as the converted pings. Matching them needs no clock offset and, unlike pick_timestamp (the later save time), identifies the target's ping exactly.

For each target, the pings of every .ss.h5 in ss_h5_dir within max_time_delta_s of the catalog time are searched for the catalog ping number (ping counters restart after recording gaps, so the time window is what makes the number unique). If the number is not there, the nearest ping in time within the window is used and recorded as position_source="catalog_ping_time".

Sets latitude/longitude to that ping's position (the vehicle position at the target ping, not the target's own seafloor position) and position_confidence="approximate", and records ss_h5 (file stem), ping_index (file-local), ping_number, position_source ("catalog_ping"), position_time_delta_s, altitude_m, ground_range_m/ground_range_clipped (from range_m), and speed_mps/meters_per_ping in extra_attributes.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default targets list of Target required ss_h5_dir str or Path

Directory of converted .ss.h5 files.

required max_time_delta_s float

Half-width of the time window around the catalog time (the catalog time has 1 s resolution).

1.5

Returns:

Type Description list of Target

Same order as targets. Targets without catalog fields, or whose catalog time is in no file (for example picked while not logging), are returned unchanged.

docs.title: project_target_to_frequency
docs.text:
project_target_to_frequency(
    target: Target,
    source_mps: float,
    target_mps: float,
    *,
    n_samples: int | None = None,
) -> Target | None

Re-express target's position on a different frequency channel of the same survey, using the one thing both channels share exactly: the physical world.

A source catalog (EdgeTech Discover, Klein SonarWiz) only ever marks a contact against the one frequency channel it was picked on — there is no "also visible on the other channel" field. But ping (both channels are pinged in lockstep — the same physical vessel position, identical ping count per channel within one file) and the physical slant range a sample represents (sample * meters_per_sample) are both real, channel-independent quantities. So the target's true position on the untagged channel is recoverable: convert its sample index to a physical slant range using the source channel's own meters/sample, then back to a sample index using the target channel's — same ping, same side, no catalog entry needed for that channel at all.

ping/channel/every other field are carried through unchanged (replace) — only sample moves, plus extra_attributes["projected_from_mps"] recording the source resolution, so a caller/renderer can tell a real catalog mark apart from one recovered this way (e.g. to draw it with a different box style) without losing the fact that it's the same real contact.

Returns None (not a clamped/guessed value) if the projected sample would land at or past n_samples — a real, physical consequence of the two channels recording different maximum ranges, not a placement bug: the contact genuinely sits beyond the other channel's recorded window and has no honest position to report there. Only checked when n_samples is given.

docs.title: correlate_target
docs.text:
correlate_target(
    target: Target,
    index: dict[Path, dict],
    max_dist_m: float,
) -> PositionMatch | None

Locate target in the surveys described by index.

The frequency channel is chosen per file with :func:match_frequency using target.extra_attributes["ping_meters_per_sample"] when present.

Strategies are tried in order:

  1. Resolved ping: a target placed by :func:resolve_targets_by_catalog_ping records its file stem (extra_attributes["ss_h5"]) and file-local ping_index; when that file is in index and the ping in range, it is used as is (distance 0). Navigation fixes often repeat over several pings, so the nearest position alone can be several pings off.
  2. Position: the nearest ping by geodesic distance on the WGS84 ellipsoid (:meth:pyproj.Geod.inv) over all files, accepted if within max_dist_m. Pings without a position fix are skipped.
  3. Ping number (only if step 1 fails or the target has no lat/lon): target.ping is a mission-global ping number, converted to a file-local index via each channel's ping_start. Accepted only when exactly one file's range contains it; zero or several candidates return None rather than guess. This recovers catalogs that carry only a pixel-derived ping and no (or a less precise) GPS position.

Parameters:

From :func:build_position_index.

Maximum distance for a position match.

docs.title: sidescanpy.viz
docs.text:
Thin plotting helpers for SideScan sonar data.

Each function renders one result onto a matplotlib Axes (creating a figure when none is given) and returns the Axes or (Figure, Axes) so callers can compose or customize it. Nothing here saves files or runs corrections: saving, multi-panel layouts and workflow belong to the caller (see examples/ and examples/figures/). Requires the viz extra (matplotlib).

Public functions
  • :func:plot_waterfall — port+starboard waterfall image with configurable x-axis (sample, ground_range, across_track, slant_range) and y-axis (ping, time, along_track) modes.
  • :func:resolve_waterfall_axes — pick x/y axis mode for a correction's step set (geometric corrections always render in real-world distance).
  • :func:plot_survey_overview — compressed, whole-survey waterfall (strided ping axis) with optional break markers at caller-supplied ping indices, e.g. file boundaries in a multi-file concatenated survey.
  • :func:plot_gridded_raster — 2D heatmap of one gridded raster.
  • :func:plot_track_and_scanlines — full-survey nadir track plus periodic port/starboard scan-line rungs, in a projected (UTM by default) coordinate system. Geometry/coverage only, no backscatter. The track comes from :func:sidescanpy.processing.build_survey_track.
  • :func:plot_track_with_targets — the same, with target catalog positions overlaid.
  • :func:plot_target_position_scatter — plain lat/lon scatter of targets.
  • :func:contact_sheet — grid of image thumbnails, one Figure.
  • :func:render_target_context — one window image with a box at a target.
  • :mod:sidescanpy.viz.analysis — one plot per analysis result (value histograms, outlier comparison, nadir zoom/waterfall, beam geometry, usable range, segments overview, navigation summary).
  • :mod:sidescanpy.viz.tvg — TVG / range-decay plots (mean vs. range, candidate fits, decay fit and residuals, fit-window limits).
  • :func:resolve_cmap — a colormap that renders NaN black, the convention every sidescanpy plot follows.
  • :mod:sidescanpy.viz.scalebar, :mod:sidescanpy.viz.basemap (maps extra) — overlays used by the map-style plots.

docs.title: sidescanpy.viz.basemap
docs.text:
Land/water context for georeferenced plots.

Two things live here: a background layer (land/water fill) to draw behind an already-projected plot (a gridded raster, a survey track), and a small standalone locator thumbnail (zoomed way out, with a marker showing where the main plot sits) — "where is this, relative to the coast." Neither one interprets or corrects backscatter; this is orientation context only.

Land geometry comes from a vendored 1:50m Natural Earth shapefile (assets/natural_earth/, public domain) — coarse by design (a coastline resolves as a smooth simplified outline, not a survey-scale shoreline). Good enough to tell "near land" from "open water" and to place a survey on a regional map; not a substitute for real chart data at sidescan survey scales (tens to thousands of meters). See that directory's own README for provenance/regeneration.

Requires the optional maps extra (cartopy) — every function here raises ImportError with a clear message if it isn't installed, rather than silently skipping the background (which could be mistaken for "there's no land nearby").

docs.text:
render_target_context(
    window: ndarray,
    target: Target,
    *,
    box_size: tuple[float, float] = (40.0, 40.0),

    vmin_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMIN_PCT,
    vmax_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMAX_PCT,
    title: str | None = None,
    coordinate_system: str = "pixel",
    resolution_m: float | None = None,
) -> Figure

Full ping-window image with a box drawn at target's computed position, for visual QA of the localization formula.

box_size is a fixed placeholder (width, height in samples/pings -- or, under a real-meters coordinate_system, output pixels of that resample, i.e. box_size * resolution_m meters) around the computed center — no real measured target dimensions exist in the source catalog (LengthMeters/WidthMeters unpopulated), so this is explicitly not derived from anything measured.

coordinate_system -- one of "pixel" (default, native sample/ping space -- export.py's raw/radiometric render levels), "geometric" (extract_geometric_window's local along/across-track meters frame), or "georef" (extract_georef_window's northing/easting meters frame) -- controls only the axis labels below; window itself must already be built in that coordinate system by the caller. Found real (2026-09-28, user report): this always labeled axes "Sample"/"Ping" even when --with-context rendered a geometric/georef real-meters resample (added 2026-09-28 to follow --render-level's own coordinate choice) -- correct-looking image, mislabeled axes.

Plot a gridded raster as a 2D heatmap.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default raster SideScanGriddedRaster

Gridded backscatter raster.

required fig Figure

Existing figure. If None, create new.

None ax Axes

Existing axes. If None, create new.

None cmap str

Colormap name.

"viridis" vmin float

Colorbar min/max. If None, use percentile-based auto-scaling (vmin_pct/vmax_pct).

None vmax float

Colorbar min/max. If None, use percentile-based auto-scaling (vmin_pct/vmax_pct).

None vmin_pct float

Percentiles for auto color scaling when vmin/vmax aren't given. Matches plot_waterfall's defaults — use the same values for both when comparing a waterfall and a gridded export of the same data, otherwise the two can show very different apparent contrast/normalization purely from differing percentile cutoffs, independent of any real difference in the underlying values (backscatter distributions with a sharp low-end density cliff, e.g. from floor-clipped no-return samples, are especially sensitive to this — a 1-2 percentile difference can shift the effective vmin by tens of dB).

Matching these two values is necessary but not sufficient for a waterfall and a gridded export to look comparably normalized: percentiles are computed over different underlying populations (every raw sample vs. every gridded cell mean), so even identical vmin_pct/vmax_pct can yield different absolute bounds — see resample_channel_to_grid()'s "Notes" section.

1.0 and 99.0 vmax_pct float

Percentiles for auto color scaling when vmin/vmax aren't given. Matches plot_waterfall's defaults — use the same values for both when comparing a waterfall and a gridded export of the same data, otherwise the two can show very different apparent contrast/normalization purely from differing percentile cutoffs, independent of any real difference in the underlying values (backscatter distributions with a sharp low-end density cliff, e.g. from floor-clipped no-return samples, are especially sensitive to this — a 1-2 percentile difference can shift the effective vmin by tens of dB).

Matching these two values is necessary but not sufficient for a waterfall and a gridded export to look comparably normalized: percentiles are computed over different underlying populations (every raw sample vs. every gridded cell mean), so even identical vmin_pct/vmax_pct can yield different absolute bounds — see resample_channel_to_grid()'s "Notes" section.

1.0 and 99.0 gamma float

Display-only power-law contrast curve, applied via matplotlib.colors.PowerNorm(gamma, vmin, vmax) instead of a plain linear scale. The plotted array is never renormalized — only the value-to-color mapping is warped — so raster stays in its real units (e.g. dB) and the colorbar (if shown) keeps honest, correctly-labeled tick values, just non-uniformly spaced. gamma=1.0 (default) is linear, identical to this function's behavior before this parameter existed.

1.0 show_colorbar bool

Include colorbar.

True show_grid bool

Show grid lines.

False show_land bool

Draw land/water context (vendored 1:50m Natural Earth data) behind the raster, in cells NaN masks out (see sidescanpy.viz.basemap) -- water-colored fill plus land polygons, drawn first so the raster paints over it wherever there's real data. Requires the optional maps extra (cartopy); raises ImportError with an install hint if it isn't installed, rather than silently skipping the background.

False show_locator bool

Add a small inset (bottom-left) showing this raster's location zoomed way out, with a marker box — "where is this, relative to the coast." Requires the optional maps extra.

False show_scale_bar bool

Draw a scale bar (see sidescanpy.viz.scalebar). Only drawn for a projected raster (raster.is_geographic False, the common case — auto-UTM-selected grids) -- a geographic raster is skipped, not drawn wrong, since meters-per-degree isn't a single constant this function can infer.

True title str

Plot title. If None, auto-generate from raster metadata, including the CRS (see _crs_label).

None

Returns:

Name Type Description fig Figure ax Axes

Axes with plotted raster.

docs.title: sidescanpy.viz.scalebar
docs.text:
A simple cartographic scale bar (line + end ticks + a rounded length label), for any plot whose axes are already in real projected meters -- this library's own default for :func:sidescanpy.viz.track.plot_track_and_scanlines (auto-UTM) and :func:sidescanpy.viz.gridded.plot_gridded_raster (auto-UTM-selected grid).

Deliberately not handling geographic (WGS84 degrees) axes automatically -- meters-per-degree varies with latitude for the x-axis specifically, so a caller plotting directly in lat/lon would need to supply the real conversion factor at that plot's own latitude, not something this function can infer from the axes alone.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: add_scale_bar
docs.text:
add_scale_bar(
    ax,
    *,
    meters_per_data_unit: float = 1.0,
    location: str = "lower right",
    color: str = "black",
    linewidth: float = 3.0,
    fontsize: int = 9,
    frac_of_width: float = 0.2,
    margin: float = 0.06,
) -> None

Draw a scale bar into ax's current view.

Call this AFTER ax's final data/limits are set (e.g. after plotting and any set_aspect/set_xlim calls) -- it reads ax.get_xlim() to size itself to the current view, so calling it earlier would size it against limits that haven't settled yet.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default meters_per_data_unit float

Real-world meters per one unit of ax's own x-axis data coordinates. 1.0 is correct for any plot already in projected meters (UTM northing/easting, this library's own default for the track/gridded plots above) -- pass a real computed value for anything else, never guess one.

1.0 location ('lower right', 'lower left', 'upper right', 'upper left')

Corner to draw in, axes-fraction positioned (robust to whatever the current data range actually is).

"lower right" frac_of_width float

Target length as a fraction of the axes' current visible width, before rounding to a "nice" value -- the actual drawn length is usually close to but not exactly this fraction.

0.2 margin float

Axes-fraction margin from the plot edge.

0.06 Notes

Does nothing (not an error) if the axes' current view is degenerate (zero or non-finite width), e.g. a single-point plot, where no scale bar length would be meaningful.

docs.title: sidescanpy.viz.track
docs.text:
Survey track + scan-line plotting.

Full-survey overview: the vessel's nadir track plus periodic "rungs" showing the port/starboard scan-line (swath edge) positions, in a projected coordinate system (UTM by default). Distinct from plot_waterfall (per-ping backscatter imagery) and plot_gridded_raster (resampled backscatter raster) — this shows geometry/coverage only, no backscatter values.

required track_lon array

plot_mean_vs_range(
    binned: DataFrame,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    *,
    show_band: bool = True,
    band: tuple[str, str] = ("p10", "p90"),
    label: str | None = None,
    color: str | None = None,
    linewidth: float = 1.5,
    zorder: float = 3.0,
    title: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]

Line plot of mean backscatter vs. range, with an optional shaded percentile band.

Call twice on the same ax (raw vs. corrected) for a direct before/after overlay.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default binned DataFrame

Output of backscatter_vs_range (or backscatter_vs_sample — any DataFrame with a "mean" column and matching min/max range columns).

required show_band bool

Shade the region between band's two percentile columns.

True band (str, str) ("p10", "p90") linewidth float

Matplotlib's own default is 1.5, so this default is a no-op for existing callers -- pass a larger value (e.g. when overlaying on top of plot_per_ping_profiles' dense low-alpha spaghetti, which can otherwise visually bury a thin mean line even with a distinct color) to make the mean line read clearly on top.

1.5 zorder float

Matplotlib draws in call order by default (zorder 1, 2, 3, ... as each ax.plot/fill_between call happens) -- 3.0 is chosen to sit above a typical single prior plot_per_ping_profiles call (which doesn't set its own zorder, so defaults to 1) even if draw order alone wouldn't guarantee it. Raise further if overlaying on top of more layers.

3.0

docs.text:
plot_per_ping_profiles(
    ds: Dataset,
    value_var: str,
    range_var: str = "ground_range_m",
    n_pings: int = 50,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    alpha: float = 0.08,
    *,
    channel_idx: int = 0,
    seed: int = 0,
    title: str | None = None,
    x_sign: float = 1.0,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]

"Spaghetti plot": overlay n_pings individual ping profiles (value_var vs. range_var, one channel) at low alpha.

Visual density shows ping-to-ping consistency/variance directly — complementary to plot_mean_vs_range's percentile band, which summarizes spread but averages away periodic per-ping artifacts.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default channel_idx int

Which channel to plot (0 = port, 1 = starboard per this schema's convention) — call twice with channel_idx=0 and channel_idx=1 on separate axes for a side-by-side port/ starboard comparison. Previously hardcoded to 0; the default preserves that exact behavior for existing callers.

0 x_sign float

Multiplies every plotted range_var value before drawing — pass -1.0 (typically for channel_idx=0/port) to mirror one channel onto the negative side of a shared axis, so calling this twice (once per channel, opposite signs) on the same ax draws one continuous full-swath profile instead of two independent one-sided ones. range_var itself (e.g. slant_range_m) is always unsigned magnitude — this is a display-only sign flip, not a different range computation. 1.0 is a no-op, preserving every existing caller's output exactly.

1.0

docs.title: plot_candidate_fit
docs.text:
plot_candidate_fit(
    fit: TVGCandidateFit,
    observed_range_m: ndarray,
    observed_loss_db: ndarray,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    *,
    color: str | None = None,
    show_observed: bool = True,
    title: str | None = None,
    use_fixed_scale: bool = True,
    model_n_points: int = 200,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]

Overlay one analysis.tvg.fit_tvg_curve() candidate's fitted model against the observed raw-loss curve it was fit against.

Call once per candidate on the same ax (result.candidates from TVGCandidateFitResult) — show_observed=True on the first call only, False on the rest, so the observed curve is drawn once and each candidate's fitted line overlays it. Mirrors plot_mean_vs_range's existing "call twice for before/after" idiom, generalized to "call once per candidate."

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default fit TVGCandidateFit

One candidate from TVGCandidateFitResult.candidates (or .best).

required observed_range_m ndarray

TVGCandidateFitResult.observed_range_m/.observed_loss_db — the same arrays for every candidate fit from one fit_tvg_curve() call, so passing a different candidate on repeated calls only changes the overlaid line.

required observed_loss_db ndarray

TVGCandidateFitResult.observed_range_m/.observed_loss_db — the same arrays for every candidate fit from one fit_tvg_curve() call, so passing a different candidate on repeated calls only changes the overlaid line.

required show_observed bool

Plot the observed curve itself. Set False on repeat calls against the same ax to avoid redrawing it once per candidate.

True use_fixed_scale bool

Draw the literal, uncalibrated model (scale pinned to 1.0) -- matches what fit_range_decay actually ranks candidates by (2026-08-24 change; see TVGCandidateFit's docstring). False draws the old free-fit-scaled line instead, for diagnostic comparison against the fixed-scale one -- e.g. to see by how much a candidate needed to cheat to look competitive.

True model_n_points int

The model line is drawn over its own dense, evenly-spaced range array from 0 to observed_range_m's max — not just at the bin centers observed_range_m happens to have — so the curve's shape reads smoothly all the way back to near-zero range for reference, including where no observed data exists (e.g. inside the excluded nadir gap). Purely a display domain; the fit itself was never evaluated there and this draws no new conclusion about that span.

200

docs.text:
set_fit_window_limits(
    ax: Axes,
    result: RangeDecayResult,
    *,
    x_pad_fraction: float = 0.12,
    y_pad_fraction: float = 0.25,
    y_pad_min_db: float = 1.0,
    x_pad_min_m: float = 1.0,
) -> None

Set robust axis limits on a decay-fit axis from the fit window.

y-limits come from the observed values inside the fit window (result.r_fit_min_m..r_fit_max_m) only, so an out-of-window outlier bin cannot compress the fit curves. x-limits deliberately span 0 to the far edge (padded), not the fit window, so a misplaced reference or window stays visible. With a shared x-axis, call this on one panel only. No-op if there is no fit or no recorded window.

docs.title: plot_range_decay_residuals
docs.text:
plot_range_decay_residuals(
    result: RangeDecayResult,
    *,
    use_fixed_scale: bool = True,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    relative_x: bool = True,
) -> tuple[Figure, Axes]

Residual (model - observed) vs. range within each candidate's fit window.

use_fixed_scale=True (default) draws the scale-1.0 residual and labels it with fixed_scale_rmse_db, the number candidates are ranked by; False draws the free-fit-scaled residual for comparison. The reference uses the nearest bin to r_ref_m, matching fit_tvg_curve's own RMSE computation exactly. relative_x=True plots distance from each candidate's r_ref_m; pass False for absolute range (to stack under :func:plot_candidate_fit on a shared x-axis).

docs.title: sidescanpy.viz.waterfall
docs.text:
Waterfall plotting for SideScan sonar.

Plots a port+starboard combined waterfall image with configurable x-axis (sample, ground_range, across_track, slant_range) and y-axis (ping, time, along_track) modes. Returns the matplotlib Axes for further customization.

2026 rshomberg@uri.edu

docs.title: plot_waterfall
docs.text:
plot_waterfall(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    start: int = 0,
    stop: int | None = None,
    x_axis: XAxisMode = "sample",
    y_axis: YAxisMode = "ping",
    ping_offset: int = 0,
    cmap: str | Colormap = _DEFAULT_CMAP,
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    vmin_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMIN_PCT,
    vmax_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMAX_PCT,
    gamma: float = 1.0,
    show_colorbar: bool = False,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    value_var: str = "backscatter_intensity",
) -> Axes

Plot a port+starboard combined waterfall.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

Validated sidescan dataset.

required value_var str

Which backscatter variable to plot -- the TVG-corrected default, or any other per-sample variable (e.g. one holding sidescanpy.processing.uncorrected_backscatter(ds) for an uncorrected view of a corrected dataset).

"backscatter_intensity" start int

First ping index to include.

0 stop int

One past last ping index. Defaults to all pings.

None x_axis (sample, ground_range, across_track, slant_range)

How to interpret the x-axis.

  • "sample": sample number, port mirrored (-N to +N). Always works.
  • "ground_range": across-bottom distance, signed by channel (port = negative). Requires ground_range_m from compute_geometric_ranges.
  • "across_track": signed across-track in platform frame (already negative for port). Requires across_track_m.
  • "slant_range": attitude-invariant time-of-flight range, signed by channel (port = negative) the same way as "ground_range". Unlike ground range, always finite (never NaN in the water column) — useful when the water column itself needs to stay visible/maskable by a caller rather than being NaN'd out by the range variable's own geometry. Requires slant_range_m.
"sample" y_axis (ping, time, along_track)

How to interpret the y-axis.

  • "ping": ping number.
  • "time": ping timestamp.
  • "along_track": cumulative platform distance from first ping. Computed via pyproj.Geod.inv from per-ping latitude/ longitude.
"ping" ping_offset int

Added to y_axis="ping" values (and to the title's ping range). Use when ds is itself an already-extracted window of a larger survey (e.g. one segment of a multi-file concatenated channel) so the y-axis reports the segment's true position in the full survey instead of 0-based local indices. Ignored for y_axis="time"/"along_track" — those are derived from ds's own per-ping fields and need no external offset.

0 cmap str or Colormap

Matplotlib colormap.

"copper" vmin float

Color scale bounds. If not given, computed from finite-value percentiles (vmin_pct and vmax_pct).

None vmax float

Color scale bounds. If not given, computed from finite-value percentiles (vmin_pct and vmax_pct).

None vmin_pct float

Percentiles for auto color scaling. Ignored if vmin or vmax is given.

1.0 and 99.0 vmax_pct float

Percentiles for auto color scaling. Ignored if vmin or vmax is given.

1.0 and 99.0 gamma float

Display-only power-law contrast curve, applied via matplotlib.colors.PowerNorm(gamma, vmin, vmax) instead of a plain linear Normalize. The plotted array itself is never modified — only the value-to-color mapping is warped — so the backscatter stays real dB and (if show_colorbar=True) the colorbar keeps honest dB tick values, just non-uniformly spaced. gamma=1.0 (default) is a linear scale, identical to this function's behavior before this parameter existed.

1.0 show_colorbar bool

If True, add a colorbar labeled "Backscatter (dB)".

False ax Axes

Axes to plot on. If not given, creates a new figure with a single Axes.

None title str

Plot title. Default: ping range and processing level.

None

Returns:

Type Description Axes

The matplotlib Axes containing the plot.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a required variable is missing for the chosen axis mode.

docs.title: resolve_waterfall_axes
docs.text:
resolve_waterfall_axes(
    steps: frozenset[str], cli_x_axis: str, cli_y_axis: str
) -> tuple[str, str]

Pick the waterfall x/y axis mode for a given correction's step set.

Corrections that include the "geometric" step always render in real-world distance (across_track x meters-in / along_track meters) rather than the caller's chosen x/y axis — otherwise the geometric correction has no visible effect (sample-index and raw ping-count axes look identical whether or not ground/across-track ranges were computed, since only the color values change from TVG, not the pixel geometry). The caller's axes remain in effect for corrections without "geometric" (raw, radiometric), where sample/ping/time are the only meaningful choices anyway.

docs.title: plot_survey_overview
docs.text:
plot_survey_overview(
    ds: Dataset,
    *,
    ping_stride: int = 20,
    break_ping_indices: list[int] | None = None,
    x_axis: XAxisMode = "sample",
    cmap: str | Colormap = _DEFAULT_CMAP,
    vmin: float | None = None,
    vmax: float | None = None,
    vmin_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMIN_PCT,
    vmax_pct: float = _DEFAULT_VMAX_PCT,
    gamma: float = 1.0,
    show_colorbar: bool = False,
    ax: Axes | None = None,
    title: str | None = None,
    value_var: str = "backscatter_intensity",
) -> Axes

Compressed, whole-survey waterfall overview.

Strides the ping axis by ping_stride before rendering (via plot_waterfall), so a very long survey renders as one reasonably-sized image instead of one row of pixels per ping. Optionally draws a horizontal marker line + ping-number label at each index in break_ping_indices — useful for e.g. file boundaries in a multi-file concatenated survey. Nothing in SideScanSurvey/ .ss.h5 currently records per-ping source-file identity, so if you need break markers, compute the boundary ping indices yourself (e.g. while concatenating per-file datasets) and pass them in here.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default ds Dataset

Validated sidescan dataset (typically a whole survey/channel, not a pre-sliced segment).

required ping_stride int

Vertical compression factor — every ping_stride-th ping is kept. Higher = more compressed. Must be >= 1.

20 break_ping_indices list[int]

Ping indices (in ds's own, un-strided index space) at which to draw a break marker — e.g. where one source file ends and the next begins in a concatenated survey.

None x_axis XAxisMode

Same meaning as in plot_waterfall. title defaults to a summary of the total ping count and compression factor.

'sample' vmin_pct XAxisMode
